<SYSTEM>This is the full developer documentation for Skribly</SYSTEM>

# Skribly documentation

> Plan the work in a tracker, let AI coding agents do it in their own worktrees, and decide yourself what ships. This is the documentation of every Skribly tool.

Skribly is a non-commercial learning project built in spare time by five developers from Rzeszów, Poland. It connects an issue tracker, a desktop environment for AI coding agents and a shared library of agent skills into one workflow. Each tool also works on its own.

Status

The product repositories are private for now and will open step by step. Pages that describe something not built yet say **planned**.

## The tools

[Section titled “The tools”](#the-tools)

* ### [Skribly Agent](/agent/)

  A desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI and nine more side by side, with tracker tasks, git, pipelines, skills, audits and a preview browser in one window.

* ### [agent-skills](/skills/)

  35 portable skills that take a coding agent from a tracker ticket to a reviewed, tested commit, with one installer for eight agents and no runtime dependencies.

* ### [Skribly Tracker](/tracker/)

  An issue tracker in the browser: projects, issues with keys such as AGENT-12, Kanban boards, comments, time logs, signed webhooks and a REST API designed for agents.

* ### [Core](/core/)

  @skribly/core holds the shared contracts, the Tracker client and webhook signing.

* ### [UI](/ui/)

  @skribly/ui holds the design tokens, the components and the site kit that give every app and every Skribly site the same look. Every component is live at ui.skribly.pl.

Short recordings of this site, with captions. They play while on screen and stop when animations are turned off.

# Accessibility

> The accessibility target of Skribly and of this documentation site, what was checked, the known limits, and how to report a barrier.

Skribly is built to **WCAG 2.2 level AA as a target**, and AAA wherever we can. Automated tools cannot prove full conformance, so this page says what was checked and how. It is a statement of intent and of known limits, not a declaration of conformity.

## This site

[Section titled “This site”](#this-site)

docs.skribly.pl is built to WCAG 2.2 AA as a target.

| What                   | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Themes                 | Light, dark and high contrast, from the theme switch in the header. **System** follows your system, including the “increase contrast” setting. The choice holds on every Skribly site.                                                                                  |
| Reader settings        | The accessibility button in the header opens a panel with text size up to 140%, grayscale, high contrast, inverted colours, a light background, underlined links, a readable font, stopped animations and a strong focus ring. The settings hold on every Skribly site. |
| Colour                 | Colours come from the `@skribly/ui` tokens, whose tests check every text and control pairing against WCAG contrast in all three themes. Links are underlined, so they never rely on colour alone.                                                                       |
| Keyboard               | Every link, the search, the menus, the theme switch and the accessibility panel work with the keyboard. `Ctrl`+`K` or `/` opens the search, and `Esc` closes it. A skip link leads to the content, and a visible focus ring marks where you are.                        |
| Structure              | One `h1` per page, headings in order, landmarks for the header, navigation, sidebar, content and footer, a breadcrumb trail, and a table of contents on longer pages.                                                                                                   |
| Motion                 | Page transitions, animations and smooth scrolling stop when your system asks for reduced motion, or when you choose **Stop animations** in the accessibility panel.                                                                                                     |
| Zoom and small screens | The layout works from 320 pixels wide and at 400% zoom without horizontal scrolling of the page; wide tables scroll on their own.                                                                                                                                       |
| Search                 | Search runs in the browser, from a local index, and is reachable with the keyboard.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Language               | Every page declares its language (English or Polish).                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Known limits:

* The [API reference](/tracker/api/) is generated from the OpenAPI description by a plugin, and its markup is less tuned than the hand-written pages.
* Screenshots have written descriptions, but they cannot show everything the app shows.

## The apps

[Section titled “The apps”](#the-apps)

| Tool            | What it offers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Agent   | Interface text size, high contrast, reduced motion, underlined links and a strong focus indicator in **Settings → Accessibility**; full keyboard control; built-in light, dark and high contrast themes. See [Accessibility in Skribly Agent](/agent/accessibility/). |
| Skribly Tracker | Light and dark themes, an accessibility panel on every page for text size, contrast, fonts and motion, and a board you can use with a keyboard by opening an issue and changing its status there.                                                                     |
| `@skribly/ui`   | Components on React Aria for keyboard and screen reader behaviour, no meaning carried by colour alone, and an axe check of every demo in every theme. See [UI](/ui/).                                                                                                 |
| agent-skills    | The `wcag-audit` skill checks your own UI against WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core and a checklist.                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Report a barrier

[Section titled “Report a barrier”](#report-a-barrier)

If something on this site or in a Skribly tool is hard or impossible to use, write to **<contact@skribly.pl>**. Tell us the page or the screen, what you tried to do, and the browser, assistive technology and system you use. We read every message, and we treat barriers as bugs.

# Skribly Agent

> A desktop IDE built around AI coding agents, not around files. What it does, what it needs and where to read more.

**Skribly Agent** is an IDE built around AI agents, not around files. It puts Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI and nine more side by side like a terminal multiplexer, with tracker tasks, git, pipelines, skills, audits and a preview browser in one window. It runs locally on macOS, Windows and Linux.

It replaces five terminals, task descriptions copy-pasted from a tracker into a chat, and one agent’s output pasted into another. It never adds a `Co-Authored-By` trailer nobody asked for.

![The Agents view: a workspace sidebar with three projects and their worktrees, and a Claude Code pane reviewing a diff](/_astro/agent-agents.DhVc-ZmU_Fwbm7.webp)

## In short

[Section titled “In short”](#in-short)

* **Agents work side by side** in tabs and split panes and tell you themselves when they are waiting for you.
* **Tasks come from your tracker as files**, not through copy-paste: `TASK.md` and `STATE.md` per task.
* **Agents hand work to each other** through state files and pipelines instead of through you.
* **Commits follow your repository’s style** and never get AI trailers, including commits made by agents.
* **Everything runs locally.** No account, no telemetry; your agents use their own logins and API keys.

## Facts

[Section titled “Facts”](#facts)

|                     |                                                                                                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Version             | 1.0.37 (6 November 2026); every push to `main` builds a new `1.0.<build>` release                             |
| Systems             | macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows 10 and 11 (x64 and ARM64), Linux x64 (AppImage, `.deb`, `.rpm`)  |
| Stack               | Electron 45, React 19, TypeScript 7, Vite 8                                                                   |
| Interface languages | Polish and English, plus any other language through online machine translation that is cached for offline use |
| Telemetry           | None                                                                                                          |
| Licence             | MIT                                                                                                           |

## Requirements

[Section titled “Requirements”](#requirements)

* `git` in your `PATH`. Without it you can preview files but not see changes.
* At least one coding agent, for example `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Skribly detects installed agents and shows the install command for missing ones.
* No separate Node.js. The app runs its helpers with its own runtime.
* `ssh` (OpenSSH) only if you want to run agents on remote machines.

# Accessibility in Skribly Agent

> Reading preferences in Skribly Agent - interface text size, high contrast, reduced motion, underlined links and a strong focus indicator - plus keyboard use and themes.

**Settings → Accessibility** holds the reading preferences for the interface. They are saved on this device with the rest of the app’s settings.

| Setting                    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Default |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| **Interface text size**    | Scales the whole interface, terminals and the editor included, in steps of 100, 110, 120, 130 and 140 percent. Terminals refit their columns and rows; pages in the Skribly browser keep their own size, so audits and agents measure the real viewport. | 100%    |
| **High contrast**          | Strengthens text and borders in the day and night themes. The terminal and code editor keep their theme colours.                                                                                                                                         | Off     |
| **Reduce motion**          | Stops transitions and animations. Until you change it, the app follows your system setting.                                                                                                                                                              | System  |
| **Underline links**        | Links stand out by more than colour.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Off     |
| **Strong focus indicator** | A thick ring around the item selected with the keyboard.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Off     |
| **Default settings**       | Restores every setting in this section; reduced motion follows the system again.                                                                                                                                                                         |         |

## Keyboard

[Section titled “Keyboard”](#keyboard)

Everything in the app can be reached from the keyboard: the command palette `⌘K` (`Ctrl+K`), view shortcuts `⌘1` to `⌘9`, and the `Ctrl+B` prefix for panes. The full list is in [Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/).

## Themes and contrast

[Section titled “Themes and contrast”](#themes-and-contrast)

* Separate day and night themes that follow the system or switch from the status bar.
* A built-in high contrast theme, **Skribly · Wysoki kontrast**.
* With any theme, Skribly picks an accent with at least 3:1 contrast against the background, and text on accent buttons with at least 4.5:1.
* Text size can also be set from 12 to 16 in **Appearance**.

## Checking your own project

[Section titled “Checking your own project”](#checking-your-own-project)

The **Audits** view runs axe-core against WCAG 2.2 A and AA on any page, and sends the findings to an agent as a task. The `wcag-audit` skill of [agent-skills](/skills/catalog/) does the same from any agent.

# Supported agents

> The 13 coding agents Skribly Agent detects and runs, how to install each one, and what each supports in panes, chat, resume, MCP and the shared browser.

Skribly runs the coding agents you already have, with their own logins and API keys. It looks for them in your `PATH` and in common install locations, and shows the install command for the missing ones in **Settings → Agents**, where each command can be copied with one click.

## Install commands

[Section titled “Install commands”](#install-commands)

| Agent         | Command        | Install                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code   | `claude`       | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`                                                   |
| Codex CLI     | `codex`        | `npm install -g @openai/codex`                                                               |
| Cursor Agent  | `cursor-agent` | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash`                                               |
| Gemini CLI    | `gemini`       | `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli`                                                          |
| OpenCode      | `opencode`     | `npm install -g opencode-ai`                                                                 |
| Copilot CLI   | `copilot`      | `npm install -g @github/copilot`                                                             |
| Aider         | `aider`        | `python -m pip install aider-install && aider-install`                                       |
| Amp           | `amp`          | `npm install -g @ampcode/cli`                                                                |
| Factory Droid | `droid`        | `curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli \| sh`                                                |
| Qwen Code     | `qwen`         | `npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code`                                                        |
| Goose         | `goose`        | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/block/goose/releases/download/stable/download_cli.sh \| bash` |
| Crush         | `crush`        | `brew install charmbracelet/tap/crush`                                                       |
| Kimi CLI      | `kimi`         | `npm install -g @moonshot-ai/kimi-code`                                                      |

After installing, click **Settings → Agents → Detect again**; the list is cached for five minutes.

Skribly also finds Claude Code when it is installed only as a VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf or VSCodium extension, in `~/.claude/local`, in `~/.local/bin` or, on macOS, bundled with the Claude app.

## What each agent supports

[Section titled “What each agent supports”](#what-each-agent-supports)

| Agent         | Panes | Chat | Native resume | MCP toggle | Shared browser |
| ------------- | ----- | ---- | ------------- | ---------- | -------------- |
| Claude Code   | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | Yes        | Yes            |
| Codex CLI     | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | Yes        | Yes            |
| Cursor Agent  | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | Yes        | Yes            |
| Gemini CLI    | Yes   | Yes  | No            | Yes        | Yes            |
| OpenCode      | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | No         | No             |
| Copilot CLI   | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | No         | No             |
| Aider         | Yes   | Yes  | No            | No         | No             |
| Amp           | Yes   | Yes  | No            | No         | No             |
| Factory Droid | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | No         | No             |
| Qwen Code     | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | No         | No             |
| Goose         | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | No         | No             |
| Crush         | Yes   | Yes  | Yes           | No         | No             |
| Kimi CLI      | Yes   | No   | Yes           | No         | No             |

* **Panes**: runs interactively in a terminal pane with state detection.
* **Chat**: runs headless in chat mode and in [pipelines](/agent/features/#pipelines).
* **Native resume**: the conversation continues after a restart. See [Resume after restart](/agent/terminals/#resume-after-restart).
* **MCP toggle**: Skribly can switch the agent’s MCP servers on and off.
* **Shared browser**: the agent can use the Skribly browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

## Custom agents

[Section titled “Custom agents”](#custom-agents)

Add your own command in **Settings → Agents**, with its arguments and, if it has one, the argument that resumes a session (`{id}`). In the CLI a custom agent is `--kind custom:<id>`.

## Skills for each agent

[Section titled “Skills for each agent”](#skills-for-each-agent)

[agent-skills](/skills/agents/) installs skills for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin, each in its own format.

# Audit rules

> What the Audits view of Skribly Agent looks for - how the score works, the secret, code pattern and SEO rules, dependency checks, accessibility checks and how findings go to an agent.

The **Audits** view looks at your project and at a running page. Security audits read your project, and accessibility and SEO audits read a running page. This page lists what each audit looks for. The view itself is introduced in [Features](/agent/features/#audits).

## How the score works

[Section titled “How the score works”](#how-the-score-works)

Every report starts at 100. Each finding lowers the score by its severity, and findings are sorted from most severe.

| Severity      | Points subtracted |
| ------------- | ----------------- |
| Critical      | 25                |
| High          | 10                |
| Medium        | 4                 |
| Low           | 1                 |
| Informational | 0                 |

## Secrets

[Section titled “Secrets”](#secrets)

The scan covers files tracked by git, up to 1 MB. The value is masked in the report, and lines that look like an example or placeholder are skipped.

| Rule                 | What it detects                                      | Severity |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `aws-key`            | AWS access key                                       | Critical |
| `github-token`       | GitHub token                                         | Critical |
| `gitlab-token`       | GitLab token                                         | Critical |
| `slack-token`        | Slack token                                          | High     |
| `stripe-key`         | Live Stripe key                                      | Critical |
| `google-key`         | Google API key                                       | High     |
| `openai-key`         | OpenAI key                                           | Critical |
| `anthropic-key`      | Anthropic key                                        | Critical |
| `private-key`        | Private key                                          | Critical |
| `jwt`                | JWT in code                                          | Medium   |
| `hardcoded-password` | A password, secret, API key or token set to a string | High     |
| `env-tracked`        | A `.env` file tracked by git                         | High     |

## Risky code patterns

[Section titled “Risky code patterns”](#risky-code-patterns)

These rules skip test and fixture folders. Every finding has a file, a line and a suggested fix.

| Rule                 | What it detects                                                       | Severity |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `eval`               | `eval(…)` in JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP or Python                    | High     |
| `new-function`       | `new Function(…)`                                                     | High     |
| `inner-html`         | HTML inserted with `innerHTML`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or `v-html` | Medium   |
| `shell-injection`    | Shell commands built from interpolated strings                        | High     |
| `sql-concat`         | SQL built from strings                                                | High     |
| `unsafe-deserialize` | Unsafe `pickle`, `yaml.load` or `unserialize`                         | High     |
| `tls-off`            | TLS verification turned off                                           | High     |
| `weak-hash`          | `md5` or `sha1`                                                       | Medium   |
| `cors-any`           | Requests allowed from any origin                                      | Medium   |
| `debug-on`           | Debug mode left on in configuration                                   | Medium   |
| `http-url`           | Plain `http://` address of an external system                         | Low      |

## Dependencies

[Section titled “Dependencies”](#dependencies)

The app reads exact versions from `package-lock.json`, `composer.lock`, pinned `requirements*.txt` and `poetry.lock`, then checks them against OSV.dev. Only package names and versions are sent, never code. Without a network, the audit still finishes with results from the rules.

## Accessibility

[Section titled “Accessibility”](#accessibility)

The page loads in a hidden window, and axe-core runs with the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 tags and best-practice rules. Each rule lists up to eight elements.

Note

axe-core finds only some accessibility problems. Check keyboard use, focus order and alternative text by hand, or with the `wcag-audit` skill.

## SEO

[Section titled “SEO”](#seo)

| Rule                                | When it fires                                        | Severity      |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `title`, `title-length`             | Missing title, or outside 15 to 65 characters        | High, low     |
| `description`, `description-length` | Missing description, or outside 50 to 170 characters | Medium, low   |
| `h1`, `h1-many`                     | Missing H1, or more than one                         | Medium, low   |
| `heading-order`                     | A skipped heading level                              | Low           |
| `canonical`                         | Missing canonical link                               | Low           |
| `lang`                              | Missing `lang` on `<html>`                           | Medium        |
| `viewport`                          | Missing meta viewport                                | High          |
| `noindex`                           | `noindex` in meta robots                             | High          |
| `https`                             | Page without HTTPS                                   | High          |
| `img-alt`                           | Images without `alt`                                 | Medium        |
| `link-text`                         | Links without text                                   | Low           |
| `og`                                | Missing `og:title` or `og:image`                     | Low           |
| `structured-data`                   | No JSON-LD                                           | Informational |
| `favicon`                           | Missing icon link                                    | Low           |
| `dom-size`                          | More than 1500 elements                              | Low           |
| `page-weight`                       | More than 3000 KB transferred                        | Medium        |
| `load-time`                         | Load event after more than 4 seconds                 | Medium        |
| `robots`, `robots-block`            | Missing `robots.txt`, or everything disallowed       | Low, high     |
| `sitemap`                           | No sitemap                                           | Low           |
| `broken:<url>`                      | Internal link with status 400 or higher              | Medium        |

## Send findings to an agent

[Section titled “Send findings to an agent”](#send-findings-to-an-agent)

Select findings and choose **Fix with agent**. A new or running agent gets a short list of up to 40 items, not the whole report, and it makes no commit.

```text
Security audit for shop found 3 problems. Fix them in the code, starting with the most severe:
1. (critical) GitHub token [scripts/release.sh:12]
2. (high) SQL query built from strings [orders/reports.py:41]
3. (medium) HTML inserted without sanitization [src/components/ProductDescription.tsx:8]
```

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)
