* [Skills catalog](/skills/catalog/): audit skills that run from any agent.
* [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/): what audits send, and where.

# The skribly command

> Control panes and agents of Skribly Agent from outside the window with the skribly command - commands, exit codes, recipes for reviewers and parallel worktrees, and safety.

The `skribly` command lets agents, scripts and you control panes from outside the window. An agent can start a reviewer next to itself, wait for it and read the result. The MCP server, `skribly mcp`, exposes the same operations to agents as MCP tools; it is described on its own page, which is planned.

## How it works

[Section titled “How it works”](#how-it-works)

* A control API runs inside the app and listens only on `127.0.0.1`, on a random free port.
* The port and a random token are written to `~/.skribly/control.json`, readable only by you. Requests without a valid token get `401`.
* `skribly` is a Node script with no dependencies. It works only while the app is running.
* Sessions started this way appear in the **Agents** view like any other.

## Turn it on

[Section titled “Turn it on”](#turn-it-on)

1. Open **Settings → Sessions & control → Local control API**. It is on by default.
2. Under **skribly command**, choose **Install** to add the command to your `PATH`.
3. Optionally install the `skribly` skill in a project. It teaches Claude Code and Codex when and how to delegate work.

## Commands

[Section titled “Commands”](#commands)

Commands take a target: a session name such as `reviewer`, a pane id, or `current` for the pane you are calling from. Every command prints JSON, and `--text` prints plain text for `read` and `explain`.

| Command                    | What it does                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `skribly status`           | Number of panes and agents, and their states                 |
| `skribly workspace list`   | Projects, worktrees and the panes in each                    |
| `skribly pane list`        | All panes, shells and agents                                 |
| `skribly pane create`      | Opens a new pane                                             |
| `skribly pane run`         | Types a shell command and Enter                              |
| `skribly pane read`        | Reads the screen as text                                     |
| `skribly pane wait-output` | Waits until output matches a regular expression              |
| `skribly pane rename`      | Names a pane for the API                                     |
| `skribly pane close`       | Closes a pane                                                |
| `skribly agent list`       | Agents and their states                                      |
| `skribly agent start`      | Starts a named agent in a new pane, optionally in a worktree |
| `skribly agent prompt`     | Sends a message, and can wait for the end of the turn        |
| `skribly agent read`       | Reads the agent’s screen                                     |
| `skribly agent wait`       | Waits for chosen states                                      |
| `skribly agent explain`    | Shows why the agent is in its state                          |
| `skribly agent stop`       | Closes the agent’s pane                                      |
| `skribly worktree list`    | Lists a project’s worktrees                                  |
| `skribly worktree create`  | Creates a worktree                                           |
| `skribly worktree remove`  | Removes a worktree and keeps the branch                      |
| `skribly notify`           | Sends a system notification                                  |
| `skribly mcp`              | Runs the MCP server                                          |

| Code  | Meaning                          |
| ----- | -------------------------------- |
| `0`   | Success                          |
| `1`   | Error, such as an unknown target |
| `2`   | Bad usage or no connection       |
| `124` | Timeout exceeded                 |

## Recipes

[Section titled “Recipes”](#recipes)

### A reviewer next to the implementer

[Section titled “A reviewer next to the implementer”](#a-reviewer-next-to-the-implementer)

```bash
skribly agent start reviewer --kind claude --prompt "Review the changes from git diff."
skribly agent wait reviewer --until done --timeout 600
skribly agent read reviewer --lines 60 --text
```

### Parallel worktrees

[Section titled “Parallel worktrees”](#parallel-worktrees)

Each agent gets its own directory and branch, so they do not overwrite each other’s files.

```bash
skribly agent start impl-api --kind codex --worktree feature/api-export --prompt "Build the CSV export endpoint per SPEC.md"
skribly agent start impl-ui --kind claude --worktree feature/ui-export --prompt "Build the export button per SPEC.md"
skribly agent wait impl-api --until finished --timeout 1800
skribly agent wait impl-ui --until finished --timeout 1800
```

### Wait, then react

[Section titled “Wait, then react”](#wait-then-react)

`blocked` means the agent is asking for permission or a choice.

```bash
skribly agent wait impl-api --until done,blocked --timeout 900
skribly agent explain impl-api --text
skribly agent read impl-api --lines 30 --text
skribly agent prompt impl-api "1"
```

### Wait for a shell command

[Section titled “Wait for a shell command”](#wait-for-a-shell-command)

```bash
skribly pane create tests --kind shell
skribly pane run tests npm test
skribly pane wait-output tests "Tests:.*(passed|failed)" --timeout 300 --new
```

## Safety

[Section titled “Safety”](#safety)

Other system users cannot read `control.json`, but any process of your own user can. If you do not use the API, turn it off with its switch in **Settings**. The ports the app opens are listed in [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/#ports).

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/): pane, app and editor keys.
* [Data and network](/agent/data-and-network/): what listens and who can reach it.
* [Features](/agent/features/): the CLI in the context of the other views.

# Data and network

> What Skribly Agent, Skribly Tracker and agent-skills store, which destinations they connect to, which ports Skribly Agent opens and how the apps protect you.

What the Skribly apps store, where it goes and which ports they open. Skribly Agent sends no telemetry and has no server of its own.

## What Skribly Agent stores

[Section titled “What Skribly Agent stores”](#what-skribly-agent-stores)

| Data                                     | Where                                | Protection                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tracker tokens                           | `secrets.json` in the data directory | Encrypted with the system password store. If that is not available, they stay in memory only |
| Tracker accounts                         | `trackers.json`                      | Plain JSON, no keys                                                                          |
| Settings, projects, layout and pipelines | JSON files in the data directory     | Plain JSON                                                                                   |
| Disabled MCP servers                     | `mcp-stash.json`                     | Plain JSON, which can include keys from the server’s configuration                           |
| Sign-ins in browser tabs                 | Separate browser profiles            | Browser cookies                                                                              |
| Task content                             | `.skribly/tasks/` in the project     | Excluded from git                                                                            |
| Control API token                        | `~/.skribly/control.json`            | Readable only by you, and new on every startup                                               |

Note

Agent sessions started by the app receive tracker tokens as environment variables, so skills can fetch tasks. An agent can read them, like any program in your terminal.

The data directory opens from **Settings → Updates → Data directory → Show**; see [Settings](/agent/settings/#data-directory).

## Where Skribly Agent connects

[Section titled “Where Skribly Agent connects”](#where-skribly-agent-connects)

It sends no statistics, crash reports or identifiers. It connects only to these destinations:

| Destination          | When                                              | What is sent                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Your trackers        | Task list, details, connection test               | Token and task queries      |
| `api.osv.dev`        | Security audit with lockfiles                     | Package names and versions  |
| `open-vsx.org`       | Searching and downloading themes                  | Search query                |
| `github.com`         | Update checks, which you can turn off             | Standard update requests    |
| Skills repository    | Download repository or Sync                       | `git clone` and `git pull`  |
| The audited site     | Accessibility or SEO audit                        | Ordinary page requests      |
| Pages in the Browser | When you open them                                | As in any browser           |
| Machine translation  | Only for an interface language that is not cached | Interface text to translate |

Programs the app runs at your request make their own connections: agents, `git push`, `ssh` and `npx` from MCP settings.

## Ports

[Section titled “Ports”](#ports)

| Port                     | Default                  | Bound to    | Who can reach it                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chrome DevTools Protocol | Off, `9333` when enabled | `127.0.0.1` | Any program on this computer, without authentication. It sees all tabs, including signed-in profiles |
| Control API              | On, random free port     | `127.0.0.1` | Processes that read the token from `control.json`                                                    |

Note

Turn on browser sharing only while you work with agents. Turn off the control API if you do not use it.

## How the app protects you

[Section titled “How the app protects you”](#how-the-app-protects-you)

* The interface has no access to Node.js and can call only a fixed list of methods.
* Preview and agent tabs run without any access to the app.
* Commands run without a shell, with a time limit and an output limit. The exception is `.cmd` and `.bat` files on Windows.
* Reading, writing, discarding and searching reject paths outside the project directory.
* Extracting packages rejects paths that escape the target directory.
* Themes are read as JSON, and extension code never runs.

Note

Agent terminals run with your permissions. An agent in a terminal can do whatever you can do in a terminal.

## Skribly Tracker

[Section titled “Skribly Tracker”](#skribly-tracker)

* Markdown is rendered with raw HTML escaped and unsafe links dropped.
* Attachments stay on a private disk and are served only through authorised routes.
* Webhook secrets and API tokens are shown once and never logged.
* A viewer’s token never changes data.

## agent-skills

[Section titled “agent-skills”](#agent-skills)

* The command line talks only to your tracker, and to OSV.dev or PageSpeed Insights when you run those audits. Your package manager reaches its own registries.
* Tokens are sent only to the tracker’s own host. Redirects to another host carry no credentials.
* The tracker command is read-only by default, and the same text is never posted twice.

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Security](/security/): how to report a vulnerability.
* [Features](/agent/features/): all views of Skribly Agent, grouped by job.

# Features

> Everything around the agents in Skribly Agent - the editor, git and commits, tasks and trackers, pipelines, skills, audits, the preview browser, Docker, integrations and the CLI.

Skribly Agent has one view per job, reachable from the sidebar, with `⌘1` to `⌘9` (`Ctrl` on Windows and Linux) or from the command palette `⌘K`. Agents themselves are covered in [Workspaces and panes](/agent/workspaces/) and [Terminals and sessions](/agent/terminals/).

## Dashboard

[Section titled “Dashboard”](#dashboard)

Agents at work, tasks assigned to you, recent commits and token usage. Token usage is computed locally from the session files of Claude Code and Codex; nothing is sent.

## A real IDE around the agents

[Section titled “A real IDE around the agents”](#a-real-ide-around-the-agents)

* A Monaco editor with tabs, quick open `⌘P`, search in files `⌘⇧F` (ripgrep), side-by-side diffs and a bottom terminal.
* Files changed by an agent reload automatically.
* **Agent actions on selected code** (`⌘⇧I`): Explain, Fix, Write tests, Review, sent to a running agent or a new session.
* The command palette `⌘K` reaches views, projects, actions and agents.

## Code and git

[Section titled “Code and git”](#code-and-git)

* Changes and the index, branches, push and pull, a history graph of all branches, and pull requests through the GitHub CLI.
* **Commit suggestions without a model.** The pattern is learned from your history (`feat(scope): …`, `[KEY] …`, `KEY: …`, `#123 - …`), with the language, type and scope taken from the changed files and the key from the branch name. The suggestion shows where each part came from.
* **Agent** improves the suggested message from the staged diff, when you want it to.
* **A commit hook strips AI trailers** such as `Co-Authored-By` and “Generated with…”, including from commits that agents make in their terminals. Turn it on with **Hook without AI trailers** at the bottom of the changes panel.
* Sign in to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea or Azure DevOps to see real commit activity.

## Tasks and trackers

[Section titled “Tasks and trackers”](#tasks-and-trackers)

* Jira (Cloud and Server/Data Center), Redmine, GitHub Issues, GitLab, Linear and Skribly Tracker in one list, plus local tasks. Skribly Tracker is the default tracker.
* **Start with an agent** writes the task to `.skribly/tasks/<KEY>/TASK.md`, creates `STATE.md`, a branch from your pattern (or a worktree) and launches the agent with a ready prompt, so the agent spends no tokens fetching the ticket.
* Status changes, comments, assignment, new issues, search and time logging without leaving the app, where the tracker supports them.
* Tokens are encrypted with the system keychain. Agent sessions receive them as environment variables named the way agent-skills expects, so `/task 123` works without a credentials file.

What each tracker supports in the app:

| Tracker         | Key                | Comment | Status | Assign | Create | Search | Log time |
| --------------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | -------- |
| Skribly Tracker | `AGENT-12`         | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| Jira            | `PROJ-123`         | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| Redmine         | `2047`             | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| GitHub          | `owner/repo#12`    | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | No       |
| GitLab          | `group/project#34` | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes      |
| Linear          | `ENG-56`           | Yes     | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | Yes    | No       |

`.skribly/` is added to `.git/info/exclude`, so task files never end up in a commit.

## Pipelines

[Section titled “Pipelines”](#pipelines)

A pipeline is several agents, from different vendors if you like, working toward one goal.

* Stages run in order; steps within a stage run in parallel.
* Each step is a headless agent that gets its role, the goal and the latest part of `.skribly/runs/<id>/handoff.md`, not the previous agent’s whole conversation. That saves tokens and lets you mix vendors.
* After a stage, every step’s answer is appended to `handoff.md`.
* A step marked **changes files** may edit; otherwise it runs read-only (for example Claude in `plan` mode, Codex with `--sandbox read-only`).
* Built in: *Plan → execution → review*, *Three audits in parallel*, *Fix, tests, documentation*, or your own. Progress shows on a graph whose nodes can be resized and expanded.

![The Pipelines view: built-in pipelines on the left, a running Plan, execution and review pipeline on a graph, and its steps on the right](/_astro/agent-pipelines.Dch2eKzV_Z1rH5s3.webp)

## Skills

[Section titled “Skills”](#skills)

* Skills from [agent-skills](/skills/) (`task`, `commit`, `review`, `handoff`, audits, `project-docs` and more) installed with one click in each agent’s own format.
* An agent can adapt the installed skills and `.tasks/workflow.md` to the project: check commands, base branch, branch and commit patterns, dev URL.
* A `.docs/` documentation skeleton generated from the repository.
* The skills repository is `github.com/skribly/agent-skills` by default, or your own fork in **Settings → Skills repository**.

## Audits

[Section titled “Audits”](#audits)

The **Audits** view checks a project and a running site, gives each report a score from 0 to 100 and sends selected findings to an agent as a short task list.

| Tab                  | What it checks                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Security             | Secrets (masked in the report) and risky patterns in files tracked by git; vulnerable dependencies from OSV.dev for npm, PyPI and Composer lock files |
| Accessibility (WCAG) | axe-core against WCAG 2.2 A and AA, in a separate, sandboxed browser session                                                                          |
| SEO                  | Technical SEO: meta tags, headings, canonical, `robots.txt`, sitemaps and up to 25 links                                                              |

Select findings and click **Fix with agent (N)**, or **Fix this** next to one. Every rule is listed in [Audit rules](/agent/audits/).

![A security audit with a score of 40 out of 100 and eleven findings sorted by severity, from a leaked token to version ranges](/_astro/agent-audits.jXLIbKSn_Qw4u2.webp)

## Browser

[Section titled “Browser”](#browser)

* Preview your app at phone, tablet and laptop sizes, with DevTools and a screenshot for the agent.
* Claude, Codex, Cursor and Gemini tabs in separate profiles, so each keeps its own sign-in.
* **Share browser with agents** over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, for `chrome-devtools-mcp` or Playwright MCP. It is off by default and listens on `127.0.0.1` only.

## Docker

[Section titled “Docker”](#docker)

Containers, compose projects and logs, with alerts when a container crashes or restarts in a loop.

## Claude and Cursor integrations

[Section titled “Claude and Cursor integrations”](#claude-and-cursor-integrations)

* Claude Code plugins from the Anthropic catalogue, installed and turned on or off per scope.
* MCP servers of Claude, Codex, Cursor and Gemini switched on and off with one toggle, without destroying their configuration.
* A **Claude Design → code** bridge and shortcuts to claude.ai.
* A **Cursor** tab: project rules (`.cursor/rules`), Cursor’s MCP servers and **Open in Cursor**.

## Themes, day and night

[Section titled “Themes, day and night”](#themes-day-and-night)

* Themes from your VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium extensions, or downloaded from Open VSX. One theme colours the interface, the code editor and the terminals.
* Separate day and night themes that follow the system or switch from the status bar.
* Built-in themes: **Skribly · Pergamin** (light), **Skribly · Atrament** (dark) and **Skribly · Wysoki kontrast** (high contrast).
* Skribly picks an accent with at least 3:1 contrast against the background, and text on accent buttons with at least 4.5:1, so no theme produces unreadable buttons.
* Themes are only read as JSON; code from extensions is never run.

## CLI and MCP

[Section titled “CLI and MCP”](#cli-and-mcp)

Agents can drive other agents through a local control API. It listens on `127.0.0.1` only, on a random port, with a random token in `~/.skribly/control.json` (permissions `600`).

```bash
skribly agent start reviewer --kind claude \
  --project . --prompt "Review the changes in git diff"
skribly agent wait reviewer --until done --timeout 600
skribly agent read reviewer --lines 60


claude mcp add skribly -- skribly mcp
```

| Command                                                                | What it does                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `skribly status`                                                       | Number of panes and agents and their states                                                                      |
| `skribly workspace list`                                               | Projects, their worktrees and the panes in each                                                                  |
| `skribly pane create`, `run`, `read`, `wait-output`, `rename`, `close` | Shell panes                                                                                                      |
| `skribly agent start <name> --kind <agent>`                            | A named agent in a new pane, optionally in a worktree (`--worktree BRANCH`) or on an SSH machine (`--machine M`) |
| `skribly agent prompt <target> <text> [--wait]`                        | Sends a message and optionally waits for the end of the turn                                                     |
| `skribly agent wait <target> [--until done,idle,blocked]`              | Waits for a state                                                                                                |
| `skribly agent read`, `explain`, `stop`                                | Reads the screen, explains the state, ends the agent                                                             |
| `skribly worktree list`, `create`, `remove`                            | Worktrees of a project                                                                                           |
| `skribly notify`                                                       | A notification from an agent or a script                                                                         |
| `skribly mcp`                                                          | The same operations as MCP tools (`skribly_*`)                                                                   |

Turn it on in **Settings → Sessions & control → Local control API** (on by default), and add the command to your `PATH` with **skribly command → Install**. The command only works while Skribly is running and needs no separate Node.js. Exit codes and recipes are on [The skribly command](/agent/cli/).

# Install Skribly Agent

> Install Skribly Agent on macOS, Windows or Linux, get past the warnings for unsigned builds and take the first steps.

Skribly Agent is published on the GitHub Releases page of its repository. Every release has the installers for macOS, Windows and Linux, the same files with stable names that always point at the newest version, the `.zip` packages used by auto-update, and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

Access

The repository is private for now, so release files are available to people with access. Public downloads are planned for when the repositories open.

## Pick your file

[Section titled “Pick your file”](#pick-your-file)

| System                       | Stable file name                | Notes                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS, Apple Silicon         | `Skribly-mac-arm64.dmg`         | Open the `.dmg` and drag the app to **Applications**                                            |
| macOS, Intel                 | `Skribly-mac-x64.dmg`           | Same as above                                                                                   |
| Windows 10/11, x64 and ARM64 | `Skribly-Setup.exe`             | One installer for both architectures; you choose the folder and a per-user or all-users install |
| Windows, portable            | `Skribly-Portable-x64.exe`      | No installation; does not update itself                                                         |
| Linux, any distribution      | `Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage` | Make it executable and run it                                                                   |
| Debian, Ubuntu               | `Skribly-linux-amd64.deb`       | Install with `apt`                                                                              |
| Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE       | `Skribly-linux-x86_64.rpm`      | Install with `dnf`                                                                              |

Versioned copies are named like `Skribly-<version>-arm64.dmg` or `Skribly-Setup-<version>.exe`. To check a download:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing   # Linux: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing
```

## Install

[Section titled “Install”](#install)

* macOS

  1. Open the `.dmg` and drag **Skribly Agent** to **Applications**.

  2. Launch it once. The app is not signed with an Apple Developer certificate, so Gatekeeper blocks the first launch.

  3. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll to the message about Skribly Agent and click **Open Anyway**. On older macOS versions, right-click the app and choose **Open**.

     Or remove the quarantine flag in Terminal:

     ```bash
     xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Skribly Agent.app"
     ```

  You only need to do this once; updates installed by the app keep working. The message “is damaged and can’t be opened” has the same cause and the same fix.

* Windows

  1. Run `Skribly-Setup.exe`. The one installer contains x64 and ARM64 and picks the right one.

  2. The installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click **More info → Run anyway**.

  3. Choose the folder and whether to install for yourself or for all users.

  The portable `Skribly-Portable-x64.exe` runs without installation and does not update itself.

* Linux

  AppImage, for any distribution:

  ```bash
  chmod +x Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage
  ./Skribly-linux-x86_64.AppImage
  ```

  On distributions without FUSE 2, install `libfuse2` (Ubuntu 22.04+: `sudo apt install libfuse2`, Ubuntu 24.04: `libfuse2t64`), or run the AppImage with `--appimage-extract-and-run`.

  Debian and Ubuntu:

  ```bash
  sudo apt install ./Skribly-linux-amd64.deb
  ```

  Fedora, RHEL and openSUSE:

  ```bash
  sudo dnf install ./Skribly-linux-x86_64.rpm
  ```

  The `.deb` and `.rpm` packages add Skribly to the application menu.

## Install an agent

[Section titled “Install an agent”](#install-an-agent)

Skribly runs the agents you already have. Install at least one, for example:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

The full list with install commands is in [Supported agents](/agent/agents/). After installing a new agent, click **Settings → Agents → Detect again**.

An app launched from Finder, the Dock or the applications menu gets a stripped-down `PATH`. On macOS and Linux, Skribly reads the environment from your login shell once at startup and adds `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`, so agents installed with nvm, Homebrew or `npm -g` are visible just like in your terminal.

## First steps

[Section titled “First steps”](#first-steps)

1. **The tour.** About a second after the first launch, an animated tour moves the cursor through 15 places in the app. Use `→` and `←` to step, **Pause** to stop and `Esc` to close. Replay it from **Help → Start tour** or the command palette.

2. **Add a project.** Click the project switcher in the top bar and choose **Add project…**, or **Clone from a link…** to start from a remote repository. Skribly detects the base branch, the checks, the dev URL and a branch pattern; adjust them in **Settings → Projects**.

3. **Connect a tracker.** **Settings → Task trackers → Add tracker** → choose the tracker, enter the URL and token → **Save and check**.

4. **Run an agent.** **Agents** (`⌘2`) → **New session** → pick an agent and the working copy (or a new worktree) → **Run**.

5. **Start a task.** **Tasks** → pick one → **Start with an agent**. The agent reads `TASK.md`, proposes a plan and waits for your “ok”.

6. **Commit.** **Code & git** (`⌘4`) → stage files → **Suggest** → **Commit**. No AI trailers.

Skribly lives in the system tray, with **Show Skribly** and **Quit** in its menu. Only one instance runs at a time; a second launch brings up the existing window.

# Settings

> What each section of Settings in Skribly Agent controls, from appearance and accessibility to trackers, agents, sessions, the browser, Docker and updates.

Open **Settings** from the sidebar or the command palette. Settings are saved on this device in the app’s data directory; tokens are encrypted with the system keychain.

| Section                    | What it controls                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Appearance and tour**    | Mode (system, day, night), the day and night themes, text size, and the app tour                                                                      |
| **Accessibility**          | Interface text size, high contrast, reduced motion, underlined links, a strong focus indicator. See [Accessibility](/agent/accessibility/).           |
| **Task trackers**          | Accounts for Skribly Tracker, Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab and Linear: URL, token, **Save and check**, **Test**                                      |
| **Git accounts**           | GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea and Azure DevOps sign-ins, used for commit activity and private clones                                               |
| **Agents**                 | Detection of installed agents, install commands, the default agent and custom agents                                                                  |
| **Projects**               | Per project: base branch, check commands, dev URL, branch pattern, commit pattern and language; **Detect** runs detection again                       |
| **Sessions & control**     | Restore sessions after restart, the worktree directory, SSH machines, the local control API, the `skribly` command and the `skribly` skill for agents |
| **Editor & notifications** | Editor options, system notifications and the interface language                                                                                       |
| **Skills repository**      | The agent-skills repository address, `github.com/skribly/agent-skills` by default, or your own fork                                                   |
| **Browser for agents**     | Sharing the Skribly browser over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and its port (1024-65535, `9333` by default)                                           |
| **Docker**                 | Container monitoring, alerts and the Docker context                                                                                                   |
| **Updates**                | The version, system and architecture, **Check for updates**, **Update automatically** and the data directory                                          |

## Projects in detail

[Section titled “Projects in detail”](#projects-in-detail)

When you add a project, Skribly detects its conventions:

| Setting                     | How it is detected                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base branch                 | The first existing one of `develop`, `main`, `master`, falling back to the first local branch                                                                       |
| Checks                      | `npm run lint`, `typecheck` and `test` when present in `package.json`, `composer test`, `python manage.py test`, and `pytest` when there is only a `pyproject.toml` |
| Dev URL                     | The port from `--port` in the `dev` or `start` script, otherwise `5173` for Vite and `3000` for everything else                                                     |
| Branch pattern              | `feature/{key}-{slug}`                                                                                                                                              |
| Commit pattern and language | Empty and automatic, which means detected from the history on every suggestion                                                                                      |

Removing a project from the list does not touch its files.

## Tracker accounts

[Section titled “Tracker accounts”](#tracker-accounts)

You can have several accounts, including several of the same type. Editing an account without entering a token keeps the old one. Deleting an account also deletes its encrypted token; task files in projects stay.

| Tracker                   | Address                                                               | Token                                                     |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Tracker           | Your instance, locally `http://localhost:8100`                        | **Profile → API tokens**, read and write                  |
| Jira Cloud                | `https://your-team.atlassian.net` and your account e-mail             | id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens                  |
| Jira Server / Data Center | Your server, with the e-mail field empty                              | Profile → Personal Access Tokens                          |
| Redmine                   | The home page address, without `/issues`                              | My account → API access key; the REST API must be enabled |
| GitHub                    | Empty for github.com; Enterprise: `https://github.example.com/api/v3` | A fine-grained token with Issues access                   |
| GitLab                    | Empty for gitlab.com, or your instance                                | A token with the `read_api` scope                         |
| Linear                    | Can stay empty                                                        | Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys          |

## Data directory

[Section titled “Data directory”](#data-directory)

**Settings → Updates → Data directory → Show** opens the folder that holds settings, the layout, sessions, encrypted secrets and downloaded themes. An install upgraded from the former name **Skryba Agent Workflow** keeps using its old folder, so nothing is lost.

# Keyboard shortcuts

> Every keyboard shortcut of Skribly Agent - the Ctrl+B pane prefix, the command palette, view switching and editor shortcuts.

On Windows and Linux use `Ctrl` wherever this page says `⌘`.

## Global

[Section titled “Global”](#global)

| Shortcut      | Action                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `⌘K` or `⌘⇧P` | Command palette: views, projects, **New session: \<agent>**, **New terminal**, actions         |
| `⌘⇧A`         | Agent panel on the right                                                                       |
| `⌘1` … `⌘9`   | Views: Dashboard, Agents, Tasks, Code & git, Pipelines, Skills, Audits, Browser, Plugins & MCP |
| `Esc`         | Closes the palette and dialogs                                                                 |

## Panes: the `Ctrl+B` prefix

[Section titled “Panes: the Ctrl+B prefix”](#panes-the-ctrlb-prefix)

Press `Ctrl+B`, release it, then press the key, as in tmux. The prefix stays active for two seconds, and a **Ctrl+B…** badge pulses on the tab bar. The shortcuts are caught before they reach the terminal, so they work with the focus in a pane. They do not work while a dialog or the palette is open.

| Shortcut                   | Action                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Ctrl+B` `v` or `%`        | Split right (new shell in the active pane’s directory) |
| `Ctrl+B` `-` or `"`        | Split down (new shell)                                 |
| `Ctrl+B` `a`               | New agent session next to the active pane              |
| `Ctrl+B` `c`               | New tab in the current workspace                       |
| `Ctrl+B` `n` / `p`         | Next / previous tab                                    |
| `Ctrl+B` `1` … `9`         | Tab by number                                          |
| `Ctrl+B` `→` `↓` / `←` `↑` | Focus the next / previous pane in the tab              |
| `Ctrl+B` `z`               | Maximise or restore the active pane                    |
| `Ctrl+B` `o`               | Overview of all agents with live screens               |
| `Ctrl+B` `j`               | Jump to the next agent waiting for you                 |
| `Ctrl+B` `x`               | Close the active pane                                  |
| `Ctrl+B` `w`               | Next workspace                                         |
| `Ctrl+B` `b`               | Show or hide the workspace sidebar                     |
| `Ctrl+B` `?`               | Shortcut cheat sheet                                   |
| `Ctrl+B` `Ctrl+B`          | Cancel the prefix                                      |

On macOS there are also `⌘D` (split right), `⌘⇧D` (split down) and `⌘T` (new tab).

Note

`Ctrl+B` never reaches the program running in the terminal. If you use tmux inside a pane, or a `Ctrl+B` shortcut in your shell, change the prefix in that program. The Skribly prefix is fixed.

## Editor and git

[Section titled “Editor and git”](#editor-and-git)

| Shortcut     | Where      | Action                               |
| ------------ | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `⌘P`         | Code       | Quick open                           |
| `⌘⇧F`        | Code       | Search in files                      |
| `⌘S`         | Editor     | Save the file                        |
| `⌘W`         | Editor     | Close the tab                        |
| `Ctrl+G`     | Editor     | Go to line                           |
| `` Ctrl+` `` | Code       | Bottom terminal                      |
| `⌘⇧I`        | Editor     | Ask an agent about the selected code |
| `⌘Enter`     | Commit box | Commit                               |

## Chat and the agent panel

[Section titled “Chat and the agent panel”](#chat-and-the-agent-panel)

| Shortcut      | Action           |
| ------------- | ---------------- |
| `Enter`       | Send the message |
| `Shift+Enter` | New line         |
| `/`           | Slash commands   |

## Tour

[Section titled “Tour”](#tour)

| Key   | Action         |
| ----- | -------------- |
| `→`   | Next step      |
| `←`   | Previous step  |
| `Esc` | Close the tour |

# Terminals and sessions

> Starting agent sessions in Skribly Agent - terminal and chat mode, the agent panel, resume after restart, SSH machines, broadcast and hand-off.

A session is one agent, or one plain shell, running in a pane. Start one from **Agents → New session**, with `Ctrl+B a`, from the split buttons in a pane header, or from the command palette (**New session: …**).

## New session

[Section titled “New session”](#new-session)

| Field                             | Meaning                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent                             | An agent card or **Terminal** for a plain shell. Agents that are not installed show their install command. |
| Project                           | The directory the session starts in                                                                        |
| Working copy                      | **Main**, an existing worktree or **+ New worktree…**                                                      |
| Machine                           | **This computer** or an SSH machine from settings                                                          |
| Name for the CLI and other agents | `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, for example `reviewer` or `impl-1`                                                |
| Mode                              | **Terminal** (the interactive agent) or **Chat** (headless)                                                |
| Can modify files                  | Chat only: whether the agent may edit files                                                                |
| First message                     | Sent right away; `Enter` starts the session                                                                |

In terminal mode Skribly opens a login shell (`$SHELL -l`; on Windows `pwsh` or `powershell.exe`) and types the agent command into it with the first message as an argument. Agents that do not take a message as an argument get it typed in after launch. Every session has the environment variable `SKRIBLY_TERMINAL=<id>`.

Caution

Agent terminals run with your permissions. An agent in a terminal can do whatever you can do in a terminal.

## Chat mode

[Section titled “Chat mode”](#chat-mode)

Chat runs an agent headless: each message is a separate call with the session id from the previous reply, so the agent remembers the conversation while no process runs between messages. The pane shows text, tool calls and errors.

| Key           | Action              |
| ------------- | ------------------- |
| `Enter`       | Send                |
| `Shift+Enter` | New line            |
| **Stop**      | Interrupt the reply |

| Agent        | Can modify files                | Read-only                |
| ------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Claude Code  | `--permission-mode acceptEdits` | `--permission-mode plan` |
| Codex        | `--full-auto`                   | `--sandbox read-only`    |
| Cursor Agent | `--force`                       | no flag                  |
| Gemini CLI   | `--approval-mode auto_edit`     | no flag                  |
| Copilot CLI  | `--allow-all-tools`             | no flag                  |
| Aider        | no flag                         | `--dry-run`              |
| OpenCode     | no toggle                       | no toggle                |

Amp, Droid, Qwen Code, Goose and Crush also have a headless mode. Kimi CLI works in the terminal only. Chats are kept in memory and do not come back after a restart; continue the conversation in a terminal, for example with `claude --resume`. The same headless mode powers [pipelines](/agent/features/#pipelines) and the **Agent** button for commit messages.

## Agent panel

[Section titled “Agent panel”](#agent-panel)

The panel on the right opens over any view with `⌘⇧A` (`Ctrl+Shift+A`). Each project keeps its own conversations, and they come back after a restart.

| Tool          | What it does                                                                             |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent menu    | Chooses the agent, or installs a missing one. Changing agents starts a new conversation. |
| Model         | The default model, the agent’s list, or any name you type                                |
| Effort        | Claude Code only: `--effort` from low to max                                             |
| `/`           | Commands from the agent, the project, your home folder and plugins; `/clear` starts over |
| Plugins       | Turns Claude Code plugins on and off for the next message                                |
| Paperclip     | Attaches files; you can also drop files or paste an image                                |
| Edit / Plan   | Whether the agent may change files                                                       |
| Remote        | Starts a Claude Code session with Remote Control                                         |
| Terminal icon | Continues the same conversation in a terminal                                            |

Under the message box you see the session time, subagents, context and cost, as far as the agent reports them. Agent terminals get the same tools in a bar under the pane; the bar holds back while the agent is asking a question, because text sent then would answer it.

## Resume after restart

[Section titled “Resume after restart”](#resume-after-restart)

**Settings → Sessions & control → Restore sessions after restart** is on by default.

* Tabs, splits and panes come back in their places with the same names, worktrees and tasks.
* Agents with a native session id resume the conversation and get a **resumed** badge:

| Agent                                       | Resume                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code, Cursor Agent, Droid, Qwen Code | `--resume <id>`                               |
| Codex                                       | `codex resume <id>`                           |
| Copilot CLI                                 | `--resume=<id>`                               |
| OpenCode, Crush, Kimi CLI                   | `--session <id>`                              |
| Goose                                       | `goose session --resume --session-id <id>`    |
| Custom agent                                | Resume arguments from its definition (`{id}`) |

* Other panes (shells, Gemini CLI, Aider, Amp, SSH sessions) start as a fresh shell in the same directory, with a hint showing the command that starts the agent again.

Quitting the app ends all terminal processes; there is no background server like tmux has. Continuity comes from the agents’ native resume and from state files (`STATE.md`, `handoff.md`).

## SSH machines

[Section titled “SSH machines”](#ssh-machines)

An agent can work on a server while its pane stays in Skribly.

1. **Settings → Sessions & control → SSH machines**: enter a name and an `ssh` target, `user@host` or an alias from `~/.ssh/config`, then **Add**.
2. In **New session**, choose the machine in the **Machine** field.

Skribly opens `ssh -t <host>`, changes to the session directory (or the home directory if it does not exist there), starts a login shell and runs the agent. The agent must be installed on the server. Authentication is handled by OpenSSH with keys in `ssh-agent` or `~/.ssh/config`; Skribly stores no passwords.

## Broadcast

[Section titled “Broadcast”](#broadcast)

Send one prompt to several agents at once, for example “run the tests and describe the failures”.

1. Tick the checkbox in the pane headers.
2. Type the text in the field on the tab bar (“To N selected…”).
3. Press `Enter`.

The text reaches every running pane as a bracketed paste followed by Enter. Exited panes are skipped.

## Handing off work

[Section titled “Handing off work”](#handing-off-work)

The hand-off button in an agent pane’s header passes the work to another agent without replaying the conversation.

1. **Send request**: the current agent saves its state (what is done, the next step, decisions, open questions) to `.skribly/tasks/<KEY>/STATE.md` for a task, or `.skribly/handoff.md` otherwise.
2. **Run another agent**: the new agent starts in the same directory and worktree with a prompt to read the state file and `TASK.md`, look at `git status` and `git diff`, summarise in three points and continue.

The new agent starts from a few dozen lines of state instead of a whole transcript.

# Token saving

> How agent-skills keeps the text that goes through the model small - loading on demand, scripts for mechanical work, asking before expensive actions, cheap restarts and working rules - with measured numbers.

Usage limits depend on how much text goes through the model. agent-skills keeps that small in five ways. The numbers below were measured on real projects by the agent-skills authors.

## Load on demand

[Section titled “Load on demand”](#load-on-demand)

An agent keeps only each skill’s name and description in context. The full `SKILL.md` loads when the skill runs, and reference files only when a step needs them. Every `SKILL.md` is at most 110 lines, and a check in CI enforces it.

## Scripts do the mechanical work

[Section titled “Scripts do the mechanical work”](#scripts-do-the-mechanical-work)

Fetching, parsing, counting and filtering are done by scripts that print only what the model needs. Sizes are in bytes, and four bytes are roughly one token.

| Task                                          | Raw input | Script output | Saved |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------- | ----- |
| Lighthouse report                             | 455,534   | 754           | 99.8% |
| Test log of 86 passing tests                  | 27,098    | 86            | 99.7% |
| `npm audit --json` on a 300-package app       | 20,555    | 2,126         | 90%   |
| `git log -60` to learn the commit style       | 7,415     | 739           | 90%   |
| GitHub issue and comments                     | 8,178     | 1,018         | 88%   |
| SQL log of one request with an N+1            | 4,204     | 490           | 88%   |
| `package.json` to find test and lint commands | 2,122     | 275           | 87%   |

Fetching a task again prints only new comments and changed fields. Failing test runs print the failing blocks with `file:line` and a summary, never the full log.

## Ask before expensive actions

[Section titled “Ask before expensive actions”](#ask-before-expensive-actions)

A screenshot costs about 1,000 to 2,000 tokens, so `browser-check` asks first and captures only the changed element. Local Lighthouse, full test suites and load tests are proposed, not run silently.

## Sessions that restart cheaply

[Section titled “Sessions that restart cheaply”](#sessions-that-restart-cheaply)

`STATE.md`, about 30 lines long, holds the goal, what was done, changed files, check results, decisions and one concrete next step. After a stage, clear the session and resume from the file. It is cheaper and more precise than dragging a long transcript along.

## Working rules

[Section titled “Working rules”](#working-rules)

The `token-saver` skill gives every agent the same habits:

* Search before reading, and read line ranges.
* Never open lockfiles or build output.
* Use short command forms, such as `git status --short`.
* Edit instead of rewriting.
* Put results first in answers.
* Use subagents with narrow briefs for wide searches.

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Skills catalog](/skills/catalog/): all skills.
* [Install agent-skills](/skills/install/): set up the skills.
* [Features](/agent/features/): all views of Skribly Agent, grouped by job.

# Troubleshooting

> Fixes for the most common Skribly Agent problems - agent detection, terminals, unsigned builds, Linux sandboxing, trackers, worktrees, hooks and audits.

## An agent is not detected

[Section titled “An agent is not detected”](#an-agent-is-not-detected)

**Symptom:** in **Settings → Agents** the agent shows “not installed”, even though it works in your terminal.

1. Click **Detect again**; the list is cached for five minutes.
2. Check where the agent is: `which claude` (Windows: `where claude`). Skribly searches the `PATH` of your login shell, plus `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`.
3. If you add the agent’s folder to `PATH` only inside a block for interactive shells, or in a file the login shell does not read, move it to `~/.zprofile` or `~/.bash_profile`.
4. A shell that takes more than five seconds to start cannot return its environment in time. Speed it up, or link the agent into `~/.local/bin`.
5. On Windows, Skribly does not read the shell; the agent must be in the system `PATH`. Restart Skribly after an npm install.
6. Restart Skribly after any change to `PATH`; the environment is read once at startup.

## Claude Code only in the VS Code extension

[Section titled “Claude Code only in the VS Code extension”](#claude-code-only-in-the-vs-code-extension)

Skribly finds the Claude Code binary from the VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium extensions, from `~/.claude/local`, from `~/.local/bin` and, on macOS, from the Claude app. If it does not, open the editor once after updating the extension so it unpacks the binary, or install the CLI with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. Claude plugins need a working `claude`.

## A terminal does not open

[Section titled “A terminal does not open”](#a-terminal-does-not-open)

**Symptom:** **New session** fails with an error about `pty.node`, `node-pty` or `posix_spawnp failed`.

* Check that `$SHELL` points to an existing file. Skribly runs `$SHELL` (by default `/bin/zsh` on macOS, `/bin/bash` on Linux), and `pwsh` or `powershell.exe` on Windows.
* **First characters disappear:** the agent command is typed 400 ms after the shell starts, and a very slow prompt can lose it. Start the agent by hand in the pane, or speed up the shell.

## `Ctrl+B` does not reach the program in the terminal

[Section titled “Ctrl+B does not reach the program in the terminal”](#ctrlb-does-not-reach-the-program-in-the-terminal)

That is intentional: `Ctrl+B` is the pane prefix. Change the prefix in tmux or the shortcut in your program. See [Keyboard shortcuts](/agent/shortcuts/).

## An agent shows the wrong state

[Section titled “An agent shows the wrong state”](#an-agent-shows-the-wrong-state)

Click the state badge in the pane. **Why this state?** shows the source, the rule and the screen. A program that keeps redrawing, like a clock or a progress bar, shows as *working*.

## macOS: “can’t be opened” or “is damaged”

[Section titled “macOS: “can’t be opened” or “is damaged””](#macos-cant-be-opened-or-is-damaged)

The app is not signed or notarised. Use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, or:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Skribly Agent.app"
```

## Windows: SmartScreen

[Section titled “Windows: SmartScreen”](#windows-smartscreen)

“Windows protected your PC” → **More info → Run anyway**. Antivirus software can also slow down the first terminal launch.

## Linux: AppImage and sandbox

[Section titled “Linux: AppImage and sandbox”](#linux-appimage-and-sandbox)

* **Does not start:** `chmod +x Skribly-*.AppImage`.
* **`libfuse.so.2: cannot open`:** install FUSE 2 (`sudo apt install libfuse2`, or `libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04), or run `./Skribly-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run`.
* **“The SUID sandbox helper binary was found, but is not configured correctly”**, or a user namespaces error on Ubuntu 23.10+ with AppArmor: install the `.deb` package, or as a workaround run with `--no-sandbox`, which weakens isolation.
* **Tokens do not survive a restart:** there is no keyring (gnome-keyring or KWallet), so Skribly keeps tokens in memory only. Install and unlock a keyring.

## The browser port is in use

[Section titled “The browser port is in use”](#the-browser-port-is-in-use)

**Symptom:** after turning on **Share browser with agents** and restarting, the status bar does not show it, or the agent connects to another Chrome.

1. Find who uses the port: `lsof -i :9333` (macOS, Linux) or `netstat -ano | findstr 9333` (Windows).
2. Change the port in **Settings → Browser for agents → Port**.
3. Restart Skribly and update the address in the agent’s MCP configuration.

## A tracker returns 401 or 403

[Section titled “A tracker returns 401 or 403”](#a-tracker-returns-401-or-403)

| Tracker                   | Check                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Tracker           | The token has the `write` ability if you change issues, and it has not expired                       |
| Jira Cloud                | The account e-mail is filled in, and the token is an API token from id.atlassian.com, not a password |
| Jira Server / Data Center | The e-mail is empty, and the token is a Personal Access Token                                        |
| Redmine                   | The administrator enabled the REST API; the key is from **My account → API access key**              |
| GitHub                    | The fine-grained token has Issues access to the right repositories and the organisation approved it  |
| GitLab                    | The token has the `read_api` scope and has not expired                                               |
| Linear                    | It is a personal API key, not OAuth                                                                  |

“Not found (HTTP 404)” usually means a wrong address, such as Redmine with `/issues` at the end, or a GitHub or GitLab key without the repository (`owner/repo#123`).

## Git refuses to remove a worktree

[Section titled “Git refuses to remove a worktree”](#git-refuses-to-remove-a-worktree)

“contains modified or untracked files”: the worktree has uncommitted changes, and Skribly asks whether to force it. To keep them, commit or `git stash` first. The branch stays either way. “is locked”: run `git worktree unlock <path>`. “is not a working tree”: the folder was deleted by hand; `git worktree prune` cleans up.

## The task branch was not created

[Section titled “The task branch was not created”](#the-task-branch-was-not-created)

**Start with an agent** creates a branch only in a clean repository; untracked files do not matter. Commit or stash, then start again. `TASK.md` and `STATE.md` are created anyway.

## The hook without AI trailers does nothing

[Section titled “The hook without AI trailers does nothing”](#the-hook-without-ai-trailers-does-nothing)

* The repository uses `core.hooksPath` (husky, lefthook), so git does not read `.git/hooks`. Add the clean-up to your own `commit-msg` hook.
* A commit with `--no-verify` skips hooks.

## The Agent button for commits is disabled

[Section titled “The Agent button for commits is disabled”](#the-agent-button-for-commits-is-disabled)

It needs staged files and an agent with a headless mode: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, Copilot or Aider.

## A WCAG or SEO audit says the page did not load within 30 seconds

[Section titled “A WCAG or SEO audit says the page did not load within 30 seconds”](#a-wcag-or-seo-audit-says-the-page-did-not-load-within-30-seconds)

Start the project’s dev server and check the address, which defaults to **Settings → Projects → Dev-mode app URL**. A page behind a login shows the login screen, because the audit runs in a separate, empty session.

## Skills do not download

[Section titled “Skills do not download”](#skills-do-not-download)

Check that `git` is in `PATH`, the network, and the address in **Settings → Skills repository**. An SSH address needs a key in `ssh-agent`.

## Still stuck

[Section titled “Still stuck”](#still-stuck)

* Find the data directory in **Settings → Updates → Data directory → Show**.
* Starting the app from a terminal shows errors from the main process. On macOS: `"/Applications/Skribly Agent.app/Contents/MacOS/Skribly Agent"`.
* Report the problem with the version from **Help → About** and your system, as described in [Security](/security/) for anything sensitive.

# Updates

> How Skribly Agent updates itself on macOS, Windows and Linux, how versions are numbered, which files each release has, and what happened to the former name.

Skribly Agent updates itself from GitHub Releases. It checks at startup and every four hours, downloads the new version in the background and installs it on the next restart.

## How auto-update works

[Section titled “How auto-update works”](#how-auto-update-works)

| When                    | What happens                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 8 seconds after startup | The first check, in a built app with **Update automatically** on                                                                  |
| Every 4 hours           | Another check                                                                                                                     |
| New version available   | Background download; the status bar shows “Downloading \<version> N%”                                                             |
| Downloaded              | The status bar shows “Version \<version> ready — restart”. Click it to install and restart, or the update installs when you quit. |
| Error                   | A message in **Settings → Updates**                                                                                               |

| System  | What updates                                                                                                     |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS   | The `-mac.zip` package. The app is not signed, so Skribly verifies the package (SHA-512) and swaps it in itself. |
| Windows | The NSIS installer. The portable build does not update itself.                                                   |
| Linux   | The AppImage. `.deb` and `.rpm` update by installing the new version.                                            |

**Settings → Updates** shows the version, system and architecture, a **Check for updates** button, the download progress, the **Update automatically** switch and the data directory.

## Versions

[Section titled “Versions”](#versions)

Versions look like `1.0.<build number>`, with release tags like `v1.0.37`. Every push to `main` builds a new version for macOS, Windows and Linux into one GitHub Release, with notes grouped from the commits and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Installed apps only see a release once it has files for every system.

## Release files

[Section titled “Release files”](#release-files)

| System  | Files                                                                                                 |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| macOS   | `Skribly-<version>-arm64.dmg`, `Skribly-<version>-x64.dmg`, plus `-mac.zip` packages for auto-update  |
| Windows | `Skribly-Setup-<version>.exe` (one installer for x64 and ARM64), `Skribly-Portable-<version>-x64.exe` |
| Linux   | `Skribly-<version>-x86_64.AppImage`, `Skribly-<version>-amd64.deb`, `Skribly-<version>-x86_64.rpm`    |

Each release also has stable copies without the version in the name, such as `Skribly-mac-arm64.dmg` and `Skribly-Setup.exe`, so a link to the latest release always gets the newest build.

## Upgrading from the former name

[Section titled “Upgrading from the former name”](#upgrading-from-the-former-name)

The app used to be called **Skryba Agent Workflow**. Updating to Skribly Agent keeps everything:

| What            | After the update                                                                                                                         |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Data directory  | An install that already uses the old folder keeps it, so settings, tokens, sessions and sign-ins stay. New installs use `Skribly Agent`. |
| Project folders | New work goes to `.skribly/`. Tasks already in `.skryba/` stay there and are still listed and resumed.                                   |
| Home folder     | `~/.skribly/control.json` is the new location. Worktrees in `~/.skryba/worktrees` stay valid.                                            |
| Command and MCP | `skryba` keeps working next to `skribly`. MCP tools are now `skribly_*`; calls to `skryba_*` still work.                                 |
| Environment     | `SKRIBLY_*` variables come first and `SKRYBA_*` still work as a fallback.                                                                |
| Saved choices   | Themes, tracker accounts, the link scheme, commit hooks and preferences carry over.                                                      |

On macOS an updated app keeps its old location in **Applications**; only a fresh install from the `.dmg` uses the new name. If you install that way, remove the old app; the data directory stays in use either way.

# Workspaces and panes

> How the Agents view of Skribly Agent is organised - workspaces, tabs, splits and panes - and how agent states and notifications work.

The **Agents** view works like a terminal multiplexer built for agents: workspaces → tabs → splits → panes. Each pane is a terminal or a chat with an agent, with state detection, notifications and resume after restart.

## Layout model

[Section titled “Layout model”](#layout-model)

| Level         | What it is                                  | Where it comes from                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Workspace** | A project directory or one of its worktrees | A pane belongs to the workspace whose path matches its directory best. Sessions outside any project land in **Other directories**. |
| **Tab**       | A set of panes in one workspace             | **+** on the tab bar, `Ctrl+B c` or `⌘T`. Double-click a tab to rename it.                                                         |
| **Split**     | A tree of horizontal and vertical splits    | Drag the dividers with the mouse.                                                                                                  |
| **Pane**      | An agent terminal, a shell or a chat        | **New session**, split shortcuts, the CLI, pipelines or tasks.                                                                     |

Terminals live in the app’s main process, so switching views or tabs, or reloading the window, does not interrupt them. A reopened pane replays its last output. The layout is saved continuously.

When a tab has three panes, Skribly opens the next session in a new tab so panes do not get too narrow. Sessions started from outside, by the CLI, pipelines or tasks, also get a place in the layout.

## Workspace sidebar

[Section titled “Workspace sidebar”](#workspace-sidebar)

The **Workspaces** sidebar on the left (toggle with its button or `Ctrl+B b`) shows:

* one group per project, with a **main** row and one row per worktree (the branch name);
* under each workspace, its sessions with the agent’s avatar, its `@name` and its state; click one to go to its pane;
* a badge in the header with the number of sessions waiting for you;
* **+** next to a project to create a worktree, and a trash icon next to a worktree to remove it.

The state of a tab, workspace or project is the most important state among its panes, in this order: *waiting for a decision* → *done* → *working* → *starting* → *ready* → *finished*.

## Pane header

[Section titled “Pane header”](#pane-header)

| Element                 | Action                                                                |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Checkbox                | Selects the pane for [broadcast](/agent/terminals/#broadcast)         |
| Avatar and title        | Double-click to rename (`Enter` saves, `Esc` cancels)                 |
| `@name`                 | The session’s name for the CLI and MCP                                |
| Branch                  | The session works in a separate worktree                              |
| Machine                 | The session runs on an SSH machine                                    |
| **resumed**             | The pane was restored after a restart                                 |
| State badge             | Opens [Why this state?](#why-this-state)                              |
| Hand-off                | [Hands the work to another agent](/agent/terminals/#handing-off-work) |
| Split right, split down | Opens **New session** next to this pane                               |
| Maximise                | Same as `Ctrl+B z`                                                    |
| Close                   | Asks first when the agent is working or waiting                       |

## Agent states

[Section titled “Agent states”](#agent-states)

| State      | Label                  | Meaning                                                          |
| ---------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `starting` | starting               | The session has just been created                                |
| `working`  | working                | The agent is working: there is activity in its output            |
| `blocked`  | waiting for a decision | The agent asks for approval or a choice and waits for you        |
| `done`     | done                   | The agent finished its turn and you have not seen the result yet |
| `idle`     | ready                  | Result seen; the agent waits for the next prompt                 |
| `exited`   | finished               | The process has exited                                           |

States come from what the agent shows, with no plugins or hooks in the agent:

* **The agent’s screen.** Each terminal has an invisible twin that renders the same stream, so Skribly reads the rendered screen rather than raw escape codes. Each agent has rules for *waiting for a decision* and *working*, such as Claude Code’s “Do you want to…?” question or Codex’s approval dialog. Generic rules catch `(y/n)`, “Press Enter to continue” and password prompts. The rules are conservative: a false *waiting for a decision* is worse than a late one.
* **Output activity.** With no matching rule, output in the last 1.5 seconds means *working*. After 2.5 seconds of silence the turn ends: *done* if there was real work you have not seen, otherwise *ready*.
* **Agent recognition.** Skribly checks the foreground process and the screen, so a plain terminal pane where you start `codex` by hand gets Codex’s avatar and rules.
* **Viewing.** A visible *done* pane in a focused window becomes *ready*.
* **Process exit.** The session becomes *finished*.

### Why this state?

[Section titled “Why this state?”](#why-this-state)

Click the state badge in a pane header. The dialog shows the state, the recognised agent, the source (screen pattern, output activity or process exit), the foreground process, the rule that matched and the last 24 lines of the screen. A program that keeps redrawing something, like a clock or a progress bar, shows as *working*.

## Notifications

[Section titled “Notifications”](#notifications)

| Where                        | When                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Badge on the **Agents** icon | The number of sessions waiting, or working when nothing waits                                                                                                                  |
| Status bar                   | “N working · M waiting”                                                                                                                                                        |
| In-app message               | An agent you cannot see asks for a decision or finished its turn                                                                                                               |
| System notification          | An agent asks for a decision, or finished a turn after at least 15 seconds of work, while no Skribly window has focus. Clicking it opens the pane. Plain shells do not notify. |
| `skribly notify`             | An agent or a script sends one itself                                                                                                                                          |

Turn system notifications off in **Settings → Editor & notifications → Notifications**.

The agent overview shows every agent’s screen at once. Arrow keys pick a session, and `Enter` or a number opens it.

## Worktrees for agents

[Section titled “Worktrees for agents”](#worktrees-for-agents)

A worktree is a separate directory with the same git history, so two agents in two worktrees never overwrite each other’s files.

1. In the workspace sidebar, hover over a project and click **+**, or choose **+ New worktree…** in **New session**.
2. Enter the branch and the base. An existing branch is checked out; a new one is created from the base, by default the project’s base branch.
3. Click **Create**. The worktree appears as its own workspace.

| Detail    | Value                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Directory | `~/.skribly/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>`, or the folder set in **Settings → Sessions & control → Worktree directory**                                   |
| Removal   | The trash icon runs `git worktree remove` and `git worktree prune`. **The branch is kept.** With uncommitted changes, Skribly asks before forcing it. |
| Refresh   | Every 30 seconds, so worktrees created in a terminal show up too                                                                                      |

## How we work

[Section titled “How we work”](#how-we-work)

Every Skribly tool is built the same way: documented, accessible, tested, and meant to keep running after the demo. Commits follow Conventional Commits in English, without AI co-author trailers. The coding agents that work on the Skribly repositories use the shared [agent-skills](/skills/) for the task workflow, commits and reviews.

# Core packages

> @skribly/core, the shared code of the Skribly apps: Tracker API contracts and client, identity and scopes, the event envelope, app manifests, the project profile, webhook signing, problem errors, environment config, logging, translations and presets.

`@skribly/core` is the shared code of the Skribly apps. It holds the Tracker API contracts and client, identity and scopes, the event catalogue, the app registry, notifications, the audit log, the project profile, webhook signing, Hono helpers, problem errors, environment config, logging, translations and the shared TypeScript, lint and design token presets. Apps never import each other; what they send each other is defined once, here.

|              |                                                                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Version      | 0.2.0                                                           |
| Runtime      | Node.js 26; the root entry also runs in browsers                |
| Validation   | Zod 4                                                           |
| Distribution | A private package installed from Git, not from the npm registry |

## Install

[Section titled “Install”](#install)

Apps install it over SSH from the private repository:

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@skribly/core": "git+ssh://git@github.com/skribly/core.git#semver:^0.2.0" } }
```

`dist` is not committed; the `prepare` script builds it during the install. While working locally, an app in a sibling folder can use `file:../skriblyCore`, which is a symlink and runs no build.

## Entry points

[Section titled “Entry points”](#entry-points)

| Import                                          | Contents                                                                                     | Runs in a browser |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `@skribly/core`                                 | Everything marked yes below                                                                  | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/contracts`                       | Zod schemas and types of the Tracker API v1, webhook payloads, `toIso8601`, `normalizeInput` | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/client`                          | `createTrackerClient`                                                                        | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/problem`                         | RFC 9457 errors and `validate`                                                               | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/env`                             | `defineEnv` and the shared env schemas                                                       | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/i18n`                            | `createTranslator`, `preferredLocale`                                                        | Yes               |
