| `@skribly/core/i18n/node`                       | `loadLanguageLines`, `parsePhpLanguageFile`                                                  | No                |
| `@skribly/core/identity`                        | Users, organisations, memberships, personal tokens, scopes and `hasScope`                    | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/events`                          | The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the event catalogue, `createEvent`, `parseEvent`               | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/registry`                        | App manifests, `createRegistry`, `fetchManifest`                                             | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/notifications`                   | The notification schema and its mapping to the `@skribly/ui` tones                           | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/audit`                           | The audit log entry schema and `diffForAudit`                                                | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/project`                         | The project profile of `.skribly/project.json`                                               | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/schema/project.schema.json`      | The project profile as JSON Schema                                                           |                   |
| `@skribly/core/http`                            | Hono 4 helpers: problem errors, bearer auth, request ids, the manifest route                 | Needs `hono`      |
| `@skribly/core/webhooks`                        | Signing, verifying and building deliveries and signed events                                 | No                |
| `@skribly/core/logger`                          | `createLogger`                                                                               | No                |
| `@skribly/core/tokens.css`                      | Tailwind 4 design tokens                                                                     | Yes               |
| `@skribly/core/tsconfig/{base,node,react}.json` | TypeScript presets                                                                           |                   |
| `@skribly/core/oxlint/{base,react}.json`        | oxlint presets                                                                               |                   |

The root entry stays browser-safe, so a React client bundle can import contracts from it. Node-only modules have their own entry points.

The ecosystem modules (identity, events, registry, notifications, audit, project and http) are reachable only through their own entry points, so their names never clash with the Tracker contracts. Their fields are camel case; the Tracker contracts keep the snake case the API sends.

## Identity and scopes

[Section titled “Identity and scopes”](#identity-and-scopes)

```ts
import { hasScope } from '@skribly/core/identity'


hasScope(token.scopes, 'tracker.issues:write')
```

A scope is `<app>.<resource>:<action>`, such as `tracker.issues:read`. The action is `read`, `write` or `admin`, and a higher one covers the lower ones. A granted scope may use wildcards, such as `tracker.*:write` or `*:read`; a required scope never does. A membership has the role `owner`, `admin`, `member` or `viewer`, and `scopesForRole` gives each role its default scopes.

These are shared definitions. Skribly Tracker’s tokens today have the `read` and `write` abilities described in [Personal access tokens](/tracker/tokens/).

## Registry

[Section titled “Registry”](#registry)

Each app can describe itself with a manifest (its id, name, version, addresses, capabilities, the events it emits and consumes, and links) and serve it at `/api/manifest`. `fetchManifest` reads one, and `createRegistry` answers which app has a capability, which apps emit or consume an event, and where an app’s API lives.

## Project profile

[Section titled “Project profile”](#project-profile)

`.skribly/project.json` describes how a project is built and worked on: the stack, the package manager, the commands, the commit conventions and, optionally, the Skribly Tracker project. `parseProjectProfile` and `stringifyProjectProfile` read and write it, and `schema/project.schema.json` is the same profile as JSON Schema. agent-skills writes and reads this file with its [`project`](/skills/catalog/#workflow) skill.

## Notifications and audit log

[Section titled “Notifications and audit log”](#notifications-and-audit-log)

`NotificationSchema` has a `tone` of `success`, `info`, `warning` or `error`, a `title`, an optional `body` and `url`, and `readAt`; `toUiTone` and `fromUiTone` map the tone to and from the `@skribly/ui` message tones. `AuditEntrySchema` records who did what to which target, with the outcome and the changes, and `diffForAudit(before, after)` builds the changes.

## Problem errors

[Section titled “Problem errors”](#problem-errors)

```ts
import { createProblem, ProblemError } from '@skribly/core/problem'


throw new ProblemError(createProblem({ status: 401, detail: t('tracker.errors.unauthenticated') }))
```

`error.toResponse()` gives a standard `Response` with `application/problem+json`, ready to return from a Hono handler. A problem keeps `message` and `errors` next to the RFC 9457 members, so existing clients keep reading them. `problemFromBody` reads both the old and the new shape.

## Environment

[Section titled “Environment”](#environment)

```ts
import { defineEnv, trackerEnvSchema } from '@skribly/core'


const env = defineEnv(trackerEnvSchema)
```

An empty `KEY=` line counts as unset. A failure throws `EnvError`, which names the variables and never their values. `trackerClientEnvSchema` reads `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL` and `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN`, the variables Skribly Agent passes to its sessions.

## Logging

[Section titled “Logging”](#logging)

```ts
import { createLogger } from '@skribly/core/logger'


const logger = createLogger({ name: 'tracker', level: env.LOG_LEVEL })
```

Writes JSON through pino. Tokens, passwords, secrets, cookies and auth headers are redacted.

## Translations

[Section titled “Translations”](#translations)

```ts
import { createTranslator } from '@skribly/core'
import { loadLanguageLines } from '@skribly/core/i18n/node'


const translator = createTranslator({ lines: await loadLanguageLines('lang'), locale: 'pl' })


translator.t('tracker.board.moved', { key: 'WEB-1', status: 'Done' })
translator.choice('tracker.list.results', 7)
```

`loadLanguageLines` reads an app’s `lang` folder, both `.php` arrays (parsed, never run) and `.json` groups. Placeholders, `|` plurals, `{0}` and `[2,*]` ranges, the Polish plural rule and the fallback locale are supported.

## Presets

[Section titled “Presets”](#presets)

```json
{ "extends": "@skribly/core/tsconfig/node.json" }
```

```json
{ "extends": ["./node_modules/@skribly/core/oxlint/base.json"] }
```

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@skribly/core/tokens.css";
```

`tsconfig/react.json` needs `vite` in the app for its `vite/client` types. The tokens leave out the font link, so an app adds its own. The full design system lives in [`@skribly/ui`](/ui/).

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Contracts](/core/contracts/): the schemas and the Tracker client.
* [Events](/core/events/): today’s webhook payloads and the shared event envelope.
* [How apps connect](/core/connecting/): which app talks to which, and with what.

# How apps connect

> Which Skribly app talks to which, over what, and with which credentials - and how to connect your own service to Skribly Tracker.

Apps never import each other. They talk over HTTP, and the shapes of what they send are defined once in `@skribly/core`.

## The connections

[Section titled “The connections”](#the-connections)

| From               | To                                      | Over                                                                                | Credentials                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Agent      | Skribly Tracker                         | REST API v1                                                                         | A read-write [personal access token](/tracker/tokens/), stored encrypted with the system keychain        |
| Skribly Agent      | Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab, Linear   | Each tracker’s own API                                                              | That tracker’s token, stored the same way                                                                |
| Skribly Agent      | agent sessions                          | Environment variables                                                               | `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL`, `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN` and the variables agent-skills expects for other trackers |
| Skribly Agent      | agent-skills                            | `git clone`, `skills.json`, the agent-skills CLI                                    | None for a repository you can read                                                                       |
| agent-skills       | the project                             | `.skribly/project.json` in the schema of `@skribly/core`, and `.skribly/lessons.md` | None                                                                                                     |
| agent-skills       | Skribly Tracker and five other trackers | REST APIs, read-only unless you post a comment                                      | Environment or `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env`                                                  |
| Skribly Tracker    | any service                             | [Signed webhooks](/tracker/webhooks/)                                               | A per-webhook secret                                                                                     |
| Scripts and agents | Skribly Agent                           | The local control API on `127.0.0.1`, the `skribly` CLI and `skribly mcp`           | A random token in `~/.skribly/control.json`, new on every start                                          |

## A task from start to finish

[Section titled “A task from start to finish”](#a-task-from-start-to-finish)

1. You create `WEB-12` in Skribly Tracker.
2. Skribly Agent lists it under **Tasks** through `GET /issues?assignee=me&status=open`.
3. **Start with an agent** writes `.skribly/tasks/WEB-12/TASK.md` and `STATE.md`, creates a branch and starts an agent with `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL` and `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN` in its environment.
4. Inside the session, the agent-skills `task` skill can refresh the task with `agent-skills tasks fetch WEB-12`, which prints only what changed.
5. The agent works, runs the checks and commits after your OK, with no AI trailers.
6. Skribly Agent posts a comment, sets the status and logs time through the API.
7. Each change makes the Tracker send `comment.created` and `issue.updated` webhooks to any service that listens.

## Connect your own service

[Section titled “Connect your own service”](#connect-your-own-service)

To read or change issues, use the REST API with a token, or `@skribly/core` in Node.js and browsers:

```ts
import { createTrackerClient, defineEnv, trackerClientEnvSchema } from '@skribly/core'


const env = defineEnv(trackerClientEnvSchema)
const tracker = createTrackerClient({ baseUrl: env.SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL, token: env.SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN })


for (const issue of (await tracker.mine()).data) console.log(issue.key, issue.title)
```

To react to changes, add a webhook and verify each delivery:

```ts
import { parseWebhookBody, verifyWebhookRequest } from '@skribly/core/webhooks'


app.post('/hooks/skribly', async (c) => {
  const raw = await c.req.text()
  if (!verifyWebhookRequest(raw, c.req.raw.headers, process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET!)) return c.body(null, 401)
  const delivery = parseWebhookBody(raw)
  queueMicrotask(() => handle(delivery))
  return c.body(null, 204)
})
```

Without `@skribly/core`, any language works: see the verification snippets in [Webhooks and signing](/tracker/webhooks/#verify-the-signature).

## Planned

[Section titled “Planned”](#planned)

* **One sign-in.** One account per person with organisations and roles, and apps signing in through OAuth 2.1.
* **Scoped app tokens.** Short-lived tokens for apps and agents, limited to chosen projects and actions. The scope format is defined in [`@skribly/core`](/core/#identity-and-scopes); no app issues such tokens yet.
* **One event stream.** The envelope is defined; apps sending it is planned. See [Events](/core/events/#the-shared-event-envelope).
* **An MCP server in the Tracker**, so any agent can use it without custom code.
* **Skribly Agent and agent-skills on `@skribly/core`.** Both talk to the Tracker today with their own clients that follow the same API; moving them onto the shared package is planned.

See [Ecosystem architecture](/overview/architecture/#planned-building-blocks) for the whole list.

# Contracts and the Tracker client

> The Zod schemas of the Skribly Tracker API v1 in @skribly/core, input normalisation and validation, and the typed Tracker client with its error types.

The contracts are Zod 4 schemas of everything the Tracker API v1 sends and accepts. Schemas are named `<Thing>Schema`, with a matching type. Every field name is the one the API sends, snake case included.

## Schemas

[Section titled “Schemas”](#schemas)

| Group          | Schemas                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enumerations   | `IssueTypeSchema`, `PrioritySchema`, `RoleSchema`, `StatusCategorySchema`, `TimeActivitySchema`, `TokenAbilitySchema`, `LocaleSchema`, `IssueSortSchema`, `WebhookEventSchema`                                       |
| People         | `PersonSchema`, `UserRefSchema`, `UserSchema`, `MeSchema`                                                                                                                                                            |
| Projects       | `ProjectSchema`, `ProjectLabelSchema`, `StatusSchema`, `TransitionSchema`, `CreateMetaSchema`, `WorkspaceRefSchema`                                                                                                  |
| Issues         | `IssueSchema`, `IssueStatusSchema`, `IssueProjectSchema`, `IssueParentSchema`, `SubtaskSchema`, `IssuePageSchema`                                                                                                    |
| Work on issues | `CommentSchema`, `AttachmentSchema`, `TimeEntrySchema`, `TimeActivityOptionSchema`                                                                                                                                   |
| Webhooks       | `WebhookSchema`, `CreatedWebhookSchema`, `WebhookDeliverySchema`                                                                                                                                                     |
| Pagination     | `PaginationMetaSchema`, `PaginationLinksSchema`                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Inputs         | `CreateIssueInputSchema`, `UpdateIssueInputSchema`, `SetStatusInputSchema`, `AssignInputSchema`, `CommentInputSchema`, `LogTimeInputSchema`, `CreateWebhookInputSchema`, `IssueListQuerySchema`, `SearchQuerySchema` |

The value lists behind the enumerations are exported too:

| Constant            | Values                                                               |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ISSUE_TYPES`       | `task`, `bug`, `feature`                                             |
| `PRIORITIES`        | `lowest`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`                          |
| `ROLES`             | `admin`, `member`, `viewer`                                          |
| `STATUS_CATEGORIES` | `todo`, `in_progress`, `done`                                        |
| `TIME_ACTIVITIES`   | `development`, `review`, `testing`, `design`, `meeting`, `other`     |
| `TOKEN_ABILITIES`   | `read`, `write`                                                      |
| `LOCALES`           | `en`, `pl`                                                           |
| `WEBHOOK_EVENTS`    | `issue.created`, `issue.updated`, `issue.deleted`, `comment.created` |

Defaults: priority `medium`, time activity `development`, sort `-updated`, 25 items per page.

## Validating input on a server

[Section titled “Validating input on a server”](#validating-input-on-a-server)

```ts
import { CreateIssueInputSchema, normalizeInput } from '@skribly/core'
import { validate } from '@skribly/core/problem'


const input = validate(CreateIssueInputSchema, normalizeInput(await request.json()))
```

`normalizeInput` trims strings and turns empty strings into `null`, as the released Tracker does. `validate` throws a `ProblemError` with status 422 whose messages read like the Tracker’s own. Pass `{ translate }` so a line such as `tracker.errors.bad_date` is translated. `toIso8601` formats timestamps with an offset, the way the API sends them.

## The Tracker client

[Section titled “The Tracker client”](#the-tracker-client)

```ts
import { createTrackerClient, ProblemError } from '@skribly/core'


const tracker = createTrackerClient({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:8100', token })


const me = await tracker.whoami()
const page = await tracker.mine()
await tracker.setStatus('WEB-3', 'Done')
```

Methods are named after the `operationId`s of the Tracker’s OpenAPI description, plus `mine()`. They are the operations listed in the [API reference](/tracker/api/), for example `getIssue`, `createIssue`, `updateIssue`, `comment`, `assign`, `logTime` and `search`. They return the content of `data`, except:

* `listIssues` and `mine`, which return the whole page with `links` and `meta`;
* `downloadAttachment`, which returns the raw `Response`.

Every answer is checked against the schemas, so a client never works with data outside the contract.

## Errors

[Section titled “Errors”](#errors)

| Failure                                          | Error                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A non-2xx answer with a Tracker or RFC 9457 body | `ProblemError` with `status`, `message` and `errors`                       |
| An answer outside the contract, or not JSON      | `TrackerContractError`; turn the check off with `validateResponses: false` |
| A network failure or timeout                     | The error `fetch` raises; the default timeout is 20 seconds                |

```ts
try {
  await tracker.getIssue('WEB-404')
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ProblemError && error.status === 404) console.log('No such issue')
  else throw error
}
```

## Kept in step with the API

[Section titled “Kept in step with the API”](#kept-in-step-with-the-api)

`@skribly/core` keeps a copy of the Tracker’s OpenAPI description and language files in its tests. The tests check the client and the schemas against the OpenAPI file, and the language parser and webhook signatures against output from the released Tracker. This site builds its [API reference](/tracker/api/) from the same file, and its build fails when the copy drifts.

# Events

> The events Skribly apps send today as signed webhooks, how @skribly/core builds and verifies them, and the shared CloudEvents envelope it defines.

## Today: Tracker webhook deliveries

[Section titled “Today: Tracker webhook deliveries”](#today-tracker-webhook-deliveries)

Skribly Tracker sends four events as [signed webhooks](/tracker/webhooks/). Their payloads are defined once in `@skribly/core`, as `WebhookDeliverySchema`, a union keyed by `event`:

```ts
type WebhookDelivery =
  | { id: string; event: 'issue.created'; sent_at: string; data: { issue: Issue } }
  | { id: string; event: 'issue.updated'; sent_at: string; data: { issue: Issue } }
  | { id: string; event: 'issue.deleted'; sent_at: string; data: { issue: { key: string; title: string }; actor: string | null } }
  | { id: string; event: 'comment.created'; sent_at: string; data: { issue: Issue; comment: { id: number; author: string | null; body: string } } }
```

`id` is a UUID per delivery and `sent_at` an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset.

## Building and verifying deliveries

[Section titled “Building and verifying deliveries”](#building-and-verifying-deliveries)

```ts
import { buildWebhookRequest, parseWebhookBody, verifyWebhookRequest } from '@skribly/core/webhooks'


const { body, headers } = buildWebhookRequest({ event: 'issue.updated', data: { issue }, secret, timeZone: 'Europe/Warsaw' })
await fetch(hook.url, { method: 'POST', headers, body })


if (verifyWebhookRequest(rawBody, request.headers, secret)) {
  const delivery = parseWebhookBody(rawBody)
}
```

| Export                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `buildWebhookRequest`                            | The body, byte for byte as the released Tracker encodes it, and the headers: `X-Skribly-Event`, `X-Skribly-Signature` and the older `X-Skryba-*` pair |
| `signWebhookBody`                                | `sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>`                                                                                                            |
| `verifyWebhookSignature`, `verifyWebhookRequest` | Constant-time check of a body against a signature or a request’s headers                                                                              |
| `webhookEventOf`                                 | The event name from either header                                                                                                                     |
| `parseWebhookBody`                               | Parses and validates a delivery                                                                                                                       |
| `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_POLICY`                        | 3 tries, a 10 and 60 second backoff, and a 5 second timeout                                                                                           |

Verify against the raw body, never a re-serialised object. Queueing the deliveries belongs to the app that sends them.

## The shared event envelope

[Section titled “The shared event envelope”](#the-shared-event-envelope)

`@skribly/core` 0.2.0 defines one envelope for every event in the ecosystem, in the [CloudEvents 1.0](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md) format, with dot-delimited types named `<app>.<noun>.<verb>`.

Status

The envelope and the catalogue are in the shared package, but no app sends them yet. Skribly Tracker still sends the deliveries above. agent-skills can print the `skills.task.completed` event of a task with `agent-skills tasks event <id>`; it sends nothing itself.

```ts
import { createEvent, parseEvent } from '@skribly/core/events'


const event = createEvent({
  type: 'agent.session.finished',
  source: 'https://agent.example.com',
  subject: 'session-42',
  data: { sessionId: 'session-42', outcome: 'completed', durationSeconds: 310, finishedAt: new Date().toISOString() }
})
```

Every event has `specversion`, `id`, `source`, `type`, `time`, an optional `subject` and `data`. `createEvent` fills in the id and an ISO 8601 time with an offset, and checks the data against the catalogue:

| Type                                             | Data                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tracker.issue.created`, `tracker.issue.updated` | `{ issue }`, as in today’s deliveries                                                                                    |
| `tracker.issue.deleted`                          | `{ issue: { key, title }, actor }`                                                                                       |
| `tracker.comment.created`                        | `{ issue, comment }`                                                                                                     |
| `agent.session.started`                          | `sessionId`, `startedAt`, and optionally `projectId`, `issueKey`, `model` and `userId`                                   |
| `agent.session.finished`                         | `sessionId`, `outcome` (`completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`), `durationSeconds`, `finishedAt`, and optionally `summary` |
| `skills.task.completed`                          | `taskId`, `skill`, `outcome` (`success`, `failure` or `skipped`), and optionally `summary` and `durationSeconds`         |
| `time.entry.created`                             | `{ entry }` with `minutes`, `activity`, `date` and the issue key                                                         |

`eventFromWebhookDelivery` lifts a delivery of today’s format into an envelope, and `CloudEventSchema` reads any envelope, including types this package does not know yet.

### Sending an event as a webhook

[Section titled “Sending an event as a webhook”](#sending-an-event-as-a-webhook)

```ts
import { buildEventRequest, parseAnyWebhookBody, verifyWebhookRequest } from '@skribly/core/webhooks'


const { body, headers } = buildEventRequest({ event, secret })
await fetch(hook.url, { method: 'POST', headers, body })


if (verifyWebhookRequest(rawBody, request.headers, secret)) {
  const event = parseAnyWebhookBody(rawBody, 'https://tracker.example.com')
}
```

The body is sent as `application/cloudevents+json` and signed with the same `X-Skribly-Signature` as today’s deliveries. `parseAnyWebhookBody` reads both formats and always returns an envelope, so a receiver built on it keeps working when an app moves to the new format.

## Planned

[Section titled “Planned”](#planned)

* Apps sending the envelope: the Tracker for its issue and comment events, Skribly Agent for its sessions.
* Signing in the Standard Webhooks style, with a timestamp in the signature and secret rotation.
* One stream that feeds webhooks, an inbox, activity feeds, the audit log and search.

# FAQ

> Short answers to common questions about Skribly - what it costs, where the code is, which agents and trackers it supports, and what leaves your machine.

## What is Skribly?

[Section titled “What is Skribly?”](#what-is-skribly)

A family of tools for planning work and building software with AI coding agents: [Skribly Agent](/agent/), [agent-skills](/skills/) and [Skribly Tracker](/tracker/), with shared [Core](/core/) and [UI](/ui/) packages. See [Ecosystem architecture](/overview/architecture/).

## Is it commercial?

[Section titled “Is it commercial?”](#is-it-commercial)

No. Skribly is a non-commercial learning project built in spare time by five developers from Rzeszów, Poland. See [Authors](/authors/).

## Where is the source code?

[Section titled “Where is the source code?”](#where-is-the-source-code)

The repositories are private for now and will open step by step. The code is MIT-licensed.

## Do I need all the tools?

[Section titled “Do I need all the tools?”](#do-i-need-all-the-tools)

No. agent-skills works in any repository with any of its eight agents. Skribly Agent works with Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab and Linear as well as Skribly Tracker. Skribly Tracker’s API works with any HTTP client.

## Which coding agents are supported?

[Section titled “Which coding agents are supported?”](#which-coding-agents-are-supported)

Skribly Agent runs 13: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Aider, Amp, Factory Droid, Qwen Code, Goose, Crush and Kimi CLI, plus your own commands. agent-skills installs skills for 8: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin. See [Supported agents](/agent/agents/) and [agents for skills](/skills/agents/).

## Which trackers are supported?

[Section titled “Which trackers are supported?”](#which-trackers-are-supported)

Skribly Tracker, Jira Cloud and Server/Data Center, Redmine, GitHub Issues, GitLab and Linear, in both Skribly Agent and agent-skills.

## Do I need an account?

[Section titled “Do I need an account?”](#do-i-need-an-account)

No. Skribly Agent and agent-skills need no Skribly account. Your agents use their own logins and API keys. Skribly Tracker has its own accounts, on your own install.

## Does anything leave my machine?

[Section titled “Does anything leave my machine?”](#does-anything-leave-my-machine)

Skribly Agent sends no telemetry. It connects only to the services you use through it: your trackers, OSV.dev for dependency audits, Open VSX for themes, GitHub for updates and skills, and the pages you open or audit. Your coding agents talk to their own vendors, as they do without Skribly. See [Security](/security/).

## Why do commits never have `Co-Authored-By` trailers?

[Section titled “Why do commits never have Co-Authored-By trailers?”](#why-do-commits-never-have-co-authored-by-trailers)

Because commits should look like yours. Skribly Agent and agent-skills write messages in your repository’s style and strip AI trailers with a `commit-msg` hook, including from commits agents make in their own terminals. See [Commits without AI trailers](/skills/commits/).

## Why does macOS or Windows warn me when I install Skribly Agent?

[Section titled “Why does macOS or Windows warn me when I install Skribly Agent?”](#why-does-macos-or-windows-warn-me-when-i-install-skribly-agent)

The installers are not signed yet. See [Install Skribly Agent](/agent/install/) for the one-time steps.

## Can I run agents on a server?

[Section titled “Can I run agents on a server?”](#can-i-run-agents-on-a-server)

Yes. Add the machine in **Settings → Sessions & control → SSH machines** and pick it in **New session**. The agent must be installed on the server. See [SSH machines](/agent/terminals/#ssh-machines).

## Does Skribly Agent keep sessions running after I quit?

[Section titled “Does Skribly Agent keep sessions running after I quit?”](#does-skribly-agent-keep-sessions-running-after-i-quit)

No. Quitting ends the terminal processes. The layout comes back, and agents that support it resume their conversation natively. See [Resume after restart](/agent/terminals/#resume-after-restart).

## Can agents read this documentation?

[Section titled “Can agents read this documentation?”](#can-agents-read-this-documentation)

Yes. [`/llms.txt`](https://docs.skribly.pl/llms.txt) lists the documentation for language models, with a full and an abridged single-file version.

## How do I report a bug or a security problem?

[Section titled “How do I report a bug or a security problem?”](#how-do-i-report-a-bug-or-a-security-problem)

Security problems and accessibility barriers go to <contact@skribly.pl>. See [Security](/security/).

# Getting started

> Pick the Skribly tools you need, install them and go from a tracker task to your first commit made with an agent.

Each Skribly tool works on its own, and they work best together. This page takes you through the whole loop in about fifteen minutes. If you only want one tool, jump to its page:

* [Skribly Agent](/agent/install/) if you want a desktop app that runs your coding agents side by side.
* [agent-skills](/skills/install/) if you already use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot or Devin and want them to follow one workflow.
* [Skribly Tracker](/tracker/self-hosting/) if you want an issue tracker whose API is designed for agents.

Access

The repositories are private for now, so cloning and downloading need access to the Skribly organisation on GitHub. Public downloads are planned for when the repositories open.

## What you need

[Section titled “What you need”](#what-you-need)

| What                                                                              | Why                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `git` in your `PATH`                                                              | Branches, worktrees, commits and downloading skills                                 |
| At least one coding agent, for example `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` | Skribly runs the agents you already have, with their own logins                     |
| Node.js 20 or newer                                                               | Only for agent-skills without Skribly Agent; the desktop app brings its own runtime |
| Docker                                                                            | Only to host Skribly Tracker yourself                                               |

## The whole loop

[Section titled “The whole loop”](#the-whole-loop)

1. **Start a tracker (optional).** Run Skribly Tracker with Docker, as in [Self-hosting](/tracker/self-hosting/), and create a personal access token on **Profile → API tokens**. You can skip this step and use Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab or Linear instead.

2. **Install Skribly Agent.** Download the file for your system and install it, as in [Install Skribly Agent](/agent/install/). The first launch opens a short tour; you can replay it from **Help**.

3. **Add a project.** Open the project switcher in the top bar and choose **Add project…**. Skribly detects the base branch, the check commands and the dev URL of the repository.

4. **Connect a tracker.** Go to **Settings → Task trackers → Add tracker**, choose the tracker, paste the URL and the token, then **Save and check**. Skribly Tracker is the default; locally its URL is `http://localhost:8100`.

5. **Install skills.** Open **Skills**, download the agent-skills repository and install the skills you want for each agent in the project. Without the app, use the CLI as in [Install agent-skills](/skills/install/).

6. **Start a task.** Open **Tasks**, pick a task and click **Start with an agent**. Skribly writes the task to `.skribly/tasks/<KEY>/TASK.md`, creates `STATE.md` and a branch from your pattern (or a worktree), and starts the agent with a ready prompt. The agent reads the task, proposes a plan and waits for your “ok”.

7. **Review and commit.** Open **Code & git**, stage the files, click **Suggest** and then **Commit**. The message follows your repository’s history and never gets AI trailers.

8. **Close the task.** Add a comment, change the status and log the time from the task panel, without leaving the app.

## Without the desktop app

[Section titled “Without the desktop app”](#without-the-desktop-app)

The same loop works in any agent’s own terminal with agent-skills:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills.git ~/agent-skills
cd ~/agent-skills && npm link
agent-skills install --target all
agent-skills config attribution off
agent-skills doctor
```

Then, in a project, run `/task 123` in Claude Code, `$task 123` in Codex or `/task 123` in the other agents. The `task` skill fetches the issue, writes `.tasks/123/TASK.md`, plans, branches after your approval, implements in stages and commits after your OK.

## See it in action

[Section titled “See it in action”](#see-it-in-action)

Every page has the same search and the same way around: `Ctrl` `K` or `/` opens search, the header leads to each tool, the sidebar to its pages and **On this page** to its sections.

[![](/media/docs-search-poster.webp)](/media/docs-search.webm)Play recording

Search: Ctrl K or / on any page, arrows to move, Enter to open.

[![](/media/docs-navigation-poster.webp)](/media/docs-navigation.webm)Play recording

Navigation: the header for each tool, the sidebar for its pages, On this page for sections, and Previous and Next.

## Next steps

[Section titled “Next steps”](#next-steps)

* [Skribly Agent features](/agent/features/): pipelines, audits, the preview browser and the CLI.
* [Skills catalog](/skills/catalog/): every skill and when to use it.
* [Tracker REST API](/tracker/rest-api/): drive the tracker from your own scripts.

# Ecosystem architecture

> What each Skribly product does, how a task travels from the tracker to a commit, and which parts exist today and which are planned.

Skribly is a local-first workbench for people and coding agents. It gives them one tracker, one look and one honest record of the work, with no account needed to start and nothing leaving your machine unless you send it. Status as of 8 November 2026.

## What makes it different

[Section titled “What makes it different”](#what-makes-it-different)

* **Local first, no account.** Skribly Agent runs on your machine with no account and no telemetry.
* **Every agent.** It works with the coding agents you already use, on your own logins, through open standards.
* **The task lives in your repository.** An issue from Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab, Linear or Skribly Tracker becomes `TASK.md` and `STATE.md` in the repository, so any tool can read it.
* **A tracker built for agents.** In Skribly Tracker an agent works on an issue as a delegate, and a person stays the owner.
* **Your style, your history.** Commits follow the repository’s own style and never get AI co-author trailers.
* **Your data can leave.** The plan is that every app exports all its data in open formats, and no feature works only against a hosted Skribly server.

## Products

[Section titled “Products”](#products)

| Product                          | What it is                                                                                                                                               | Status                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Skribly Agent](/agent/)         | Desktop app that runs many coding agents side by side, turns issues into task files, and shows which agent is working, waiting for you or done           | Available, v1.0.37                                        |
| [agent-skills](/skills/)         | A library of 35 skills and a small installer for eight coding agents, in the shared Agent Skills format                                                  | Available to the team, v0.2.14                            |
| [Skribly Tracker](/tracker/)     | Issue tracker with a REST API and signed webhooks, designed for people and agents together                                                               | First release, 0.1; a move to the shared stack is planned |
| [`@skribly/core`](/core/)        | Shared contracts, API client, webhook signing, the event envelope, identity and scopes, app manifests, the project profile, errors, config, translations | v0.2.0                                                    |
| [`@skribly/ui`](/ui/)            | Design tokens, plain CSS classes and React components for one look everywhere                                                                            | First version                                             |
| [skribly.pl](https://skribly.pl) | The product site                                                                                                                                         | Live                                                      |
| docs.skribly.pl                  | This documentation                                                                                                                                       | Live                                                      |

## The workflow

[Section titled “The workflow”](#the-workflow)

```text
Skribly Tracker            Skribly Agent                     Coding agents
(or Jira, Redmine,  task   branch or worktree,       runs    Claude Code, Codex,
 GitHub, GitLab,   ──────▶ TASK.md and STATE.md,   ──────▶  Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI
 Linear)                   an agent session                  and nine more
      ▲                                                            │
      │ comment, status, time                       rules          │ changes
      │                                     agent-skills ─────────▶│
      │                                     tests, reviews,        ▼
      └──────────────────────────────────── audits, commits   You review the diff
                                                              and the audit results
```

1. **Plan.** A task starts in Skribly Tracker or arrives from Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab or Linear.
2. **Start.** One action in Skribly Agent creates the branch, saves the task to `.skribly/tasks/<KEY>/TASK.md` and starts an agent with a ready prompt.
3. **Agents work.** Each one can run in its own Git worktree, and the app shows who is working, waiting or done.
4. **Rules apply.** Tests, reviews, audits and commit style come from one skill library, agent-skills.
5. **Review.** You read the changes and the security, WCAG and SEO audit results.
6. **Close.** You accept the commit and add the comment and logged time to the task.

agent-skills needs nothing else to work: it is a standalone library for any repository and any of the eight agents it supports. Skribly Agent works with trackers other than Skribly Tracker, and Skribly Tracker’s API works with any HTTP client.

## How the apps connect today

[Section titled “How the apps connect today”](#how-the-apps-connect-today)

| From            | To                                                     | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Skribly Agent   | Skribly Tracker, Jira, Redmine, GitHub, GitLab, Linear | Each tracker’s REST API with a token stored in the system keychain. See [Tasks and trackers](/agent/features/#tasks-and-trackers).                                                                                                                     |
| Skribly Agent   | agent-skills                                           | Clones the skills repository, reads `skills.json` and installs skills per project and per agent through the agent-skills CLI.                                                                                                                          |
| Skribly Agent   | coding agents                                          | Starts each agent’s own CLI in a terminal or in headless mode, and passes `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL` and `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN` to the session.                                                                                                            |
| agent-skills    | Skribly Tracker and five other trackers                | `agent-skills tasks fetch` reads issues with a personal token. See [Trackers](/skills/trackers/).                                                                                                                                                      |
| agent-skills    | `@skribly/core`                                        | `.skribly/project.json` follows the project profile schema of `@skribly/core`, copied into agent-skills so it keeps no runtime dependencies. `agent-skills tasks event` prints the `skills.task.completed` event in the core format; it sends nothing. |
| Skribly Tracker | any service                                            | [Signed webhooks](/tracker/webhooks/) for `issue.created`, `issue.updated`, `issue.deleted` and `comment.created`.                                                                                                                                     |
| Every Node app  | `@skribly/core`, `@skribly/ui`                         | Shared packages for contracts, the Tracker client, webhook signing and the look. See [How apps connect](/core/connecting/).                                                                                                                            |

Apps never import each other. They talk over HTTP, and the shapes of what they send are defined once in `@skribly/core`.

## Shared packages

[Section titled “Shared packages”](#shared-packages)

* **`@skribly/core` connects everything.** It holds the contracts the apps speak: the Tracker API v1 schemas, the Tracker client, webhook signing and verification, RFC 9457 problem errors, environment config, logging and translations. Since 0.2.0 it also defines the shared building blocks below as schemas and helpers: identity and scopes, the CloudEvents envelope, app manifests, notifications, the audit log and the project profile. The apps do not use most of them yet.
* **`@skribly/ui` gives one look.** Three layers: design tokens, plain CSS classes for any page, and React components built on React Aria for keyboard and screen reader behaviour. A later framework change replaces only the top layer. This site uses the tokens and the plain classes.

## Planned building blocks

[Section titled “Planned building blocks”](#planned-building-blocks)

These are designs, not features you can use in the apps today. Where `@skribly/core` 0.2.0 already defines the shapes, the status says so; a schema in the shared package is not yet a feature of an app.

| Block           | Design                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Status                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity        | One account per person, organisations with the roles `admin`, `member` and `viewer`. Apps sign in through OAuth 2.1. Integrations belong to the organisation, not to whoever installed them.                                            | Planned; users, organisations and memberships are defined in `@skribly/core`                                               |
| Tokens          | Personal tokens for people writing scripts. Apps and agents get short-lived tokens limited to chosen projects and actions, and act as a visible bot.                                                                                    | Planned; personal tokens exist in Skribly Tracker today, and `@skribly/core` defines scopes such as `tracker.issues:write` |
| Events          | One envelope in the CloudEvents 1.0.2 format, with dot-delimited types such as `issue.updated`, the actor (person, agent or app) and what changed. The same stream feeds webhooks, the inbox, activity feeds, the audit log and search. | The envelope and the event catalogue are in `@skribly/core`; no app sends them yet. See [Events](/core/events/)            |
| Webhooks        | Signed the Standard Webhooks way: an id, a timestamp and a signature over both, secret rotation without downtime, and retries over about a day.                                                                                         | Planned; HMAC-SHA256 signing exists today                                                                                  |
| App manifests   | Each app describes itself in one file: name, address, navigation, commands, widgets, events and permissions.                                                                                                                            | Planned; a first manifest schema and registry are in `@skribly/core`                                                       |
| Command palette | Cmd/Ctrl+K in every app, on by default, with keyboard sequences such as G then I for the inbox.                                                                                                                                         | In Skribly Agent today; planned elsewhere                                                                                  |
| Inbox           | One list of what needs you, with a reason on each item. “An agent is waiting for you” comes first.                                                                                                                                      | Planned                                                                                                                    |
| Agent sessions  | An agent works on an issue as a delegate and reports what it is doing: thoughts, actions, questions, answers, errors and a plan. A person stays accountable.                                                                            | Planned                                                                                                                    |
| MCP             | Skribly Tracker will offer a Model Context Protocol server (revision 2026-07-28) with OAuth, a read-only mode and per-project scope.                                                                                                    | Planned; Skribly Agent already has an MCP server for driving its own sessions                                              |
| Feature flags   | One switch turns off every AI feature, and each AI feature says what it sends to a model.                                                                                                                                               | Planned                                                                                                                    |

## Open standards

[Section titled “Open standards”](#open-standards)

| Standard                                                                                                | Used for                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/versioning), revision 2026-07-28 | Tools for agents                                                                               |
| [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/overview/introduction)                          | Talking to local agents in a structured way                                                    |
| [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification)                                                    | The format of agent-skills                                                                     |
| [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md)                                                                          | Project instructions for agents                                                                |
| [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/)                                                                        | Docs that agents can read; this site publishes [`/llms.txt`](https://docs.skribly.pl/llms.txt) |
| [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/)                                                  | Signing webhooks (planned)                                                                     |
| [CloudEvents 1.0.2](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/v1.0.2/cloudevents/spec.md)                | The event envelope in `@skribly/core`                                                          |
| [OpenAPI 3.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0)                                                     | The [REST API reference](/tracker/api/)                                                        |
| [Design Tokens (DTCG)](https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/)                                 | Token files of `@skribly/ui`                                                                   |
| [WCAG 2.2 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)                                                            | The accessibility target                                                                       |

## Stack

[Section titled “Stack”](#stack)

The shared stack planned for every app, checked on 8 November 2026:

| Layer   | Choice                                                                  |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Runtime | Node.js 26 LTS (supported until 30 April 2029), TypeScript 7            |
| Web     | React 19, React Router 8, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4, React Aria Components |
| Server  | Hono 4                                                                  |
| Data    | PostgreSQL 18, Drizzle ORM, Zod 4, pg-boss for queues                   |
| Desktop | Electron 45                                                             |
| Docs    | Astro 7 with Starlight, Pagefind search                                 |
| Quality | Vitest, Playwright, oxlint, axe                                         |

Skribly Agent already runs on Electron, React and Vite. `@skribly/core`, `@skribly/ui` and this site run on Node.js 26. Skribly Tracker is being rewritten on this stack.

## Principles

[Section titled “Principles”](#principles)

1. Local first; an account is a reason to share, never a gate.
2. Open standards over closed plugin systems.
3. A person stays accountable. Agents are always shown as agents, stop when told, and never log time or push code silently.
4. Time from the work, never from watching people.
5. The task lives in the repository.
6. One identity, one shell, one palette, one inbox, one look.
7. Your data can leave in open formats.
8. Public claims are checked and dated.

## Privacy and accessibility

[Section titled “Privacy and accessibility”](#privacy-and-accessibility)

* Skribly Agent sends no telemetry. When an app sends anything, it says what and where. See [Security](/security/).
* Skribly will not offer screenshots, keystroke counts or productivity scores of people.
* The target is WCAG 2.2 AA, and AAA wherever possible. Automated tools cannot prove full conformance, so each statement says what was tested by hand. A statement is not a declaration of conformity. See [Accessibility](/accessibility/).

# Release train 0.3

> The first release train of Skribly: @skribly/core 0.3.0 and agent-skills 0.3.0, with @skribly/ui following in a later train, what each brings and how to upgrade.

The shared packages of Skribly now ship as a release train: one train per minor version, so the packages of the same train are known to work together. Train 0.3 is the first one. A fix inside a train moves only the package it fixes, as 0.3.1, 0.3.2 and so on.

| Package         | Version                             | Before |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------ |
| `@skribly/core` | 0.3.0                               | 0.2.0  |
| agent-skills    | 0.3.0                               | 0.2.14 |
| `@skribly/ui`   | follows a later train (stays 0.1.0) | 0.1.0  |

`@skribly/ui` is not part of this train: its next version waits for work on the design direction and the admin components, and it joins a later train. Until then ui 0.1.0 is the version that goes with core 0.3.0, and the sites keep the copy of the site kit they have.

Which versions belong to which train is written in `compat.json` in the core repository: the versions of the train, the packages that follow a later one, the ui commit each site uses, the oldest Skribly Agent and Skribly Tracker that work with the train, and the Node.js, Astro, React and Next.js versions it was tested on.

## Added

[Section titled “Added”](#added)

### Core

[Section titled “Core”](#core)

* **The server kit**: eight entry points under `@skribly/core/server/` with the code every Skribly server needs from its first day. `db` opens Postgres (or PGlite in tests) and runs each request in a transaction of its organisation under row-level security. `events` keeps events in an outbox in the same transaction and runs background jobs. `seed` fills a database with minimal or demo data. `app` wires the modules of an app together. `http` adds the shared Hono middleware: errors as problem details, a body size limit, idempotency keys that never run a write twice, and rate limits. `mcp` serves an app’s actions as MCP tools at `/mcp`, with writes confirmed by the person. `testing` gives isolation and cross-organisation tests. `telemetry` sends OpenTelemetry traces.
* **Contracts**: API conventions (version in the path, cursor pagination), ports with fakes for tests, Standard Schema, Standard Webhooks, the event catalogue of every product, identity with workspaces and installations, the admin API of Skribly ID (experimental), manifest v2, the product registry and catalogue, feature flags (experimental), and more Skribly Tracker operations in the contracts and the client.
* **Generated files**: a JSON Schema file for every schema and OpenAPI 3.1 files for Skribly Tracker and Skribly ID.
* **Presets**: the shared Prettier config as `@skribly/core/prettier` and an oxlint preset for Next.js apps.

### agent-skills

[Section titled “agent-skills”](#agent-skills)

* Four new skills: `newsletter`, `slice`, `seed` and `standard`. See the [Skills catalog](/skills/catalog/).

## Changed

[Section titled “Changed”](#changed)

* Core: a request can only open a transaction of the organisation it is signed in to (401 without a sign-in, 403 for another organisation). Every access check names the organisation. Dates, webhook addresses and links are checked more strictly.
* agent-skills: releases now follow the train. A release is made for a version tag such as `v0.3.0` only; the releases numbered by build (`v0.2.1` to `v0.2.14`) end here.
* agent-skills: `agent-skills agent-files` writes only `CLAUDE.md` and the Copilot pointer by default, and `--prune` removes what older versions wrote. The skill scripts never start a program found inside the repository you work in. See [Supported agents](/skills/agents/).

## Fixed

[Section titled “Fixed”](#fixed)

* Core: rate-limit headers set by a handler are kept, and every finding of the November review of the server kit is closed.
* agent-skills: `agent-files` stays inside the repository it runs in and no longer replaces your own `.mcp.json`.

## Upgrading

[Section titled “Upgrading”](#upgrading)

1. `@skribly/core` 0.3.0 is not on GitHub Packages yet: the publish runs in the release workflow, which comes later. Until then apps keep installing core from a packed tarball in their `vendor/` folder; repack it from the `v0.3.0` tag with `node .tools/pack-libs.mjs <app>` in core. `@skribly/ui` stays at its 0.1.0 tarball.
2. Once core is published, an app copies the `.npmrc` template of the core repository (`.tools/npmrc.template`), sets a token that can read packages as `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, pins `"@skribly/core": "0.3.0"` exactly, and uses the shared Prettier config with `"prettier": "@skribly/core/prettier"` in `package.json` instead of its own `.prettierrc.json`.
3. Before migrating a database, run the database setup of the server kit again: it adds a role the new migrations need.
4. Code that opened a transaction for work outside any organisation, such as a sign-in, moves to `db.identity`. Access checks pass the organisation.
5. Run `agent-skills install` again, then `agent-skills agent-files --prune` once in each repository.

# Security

> How to report a security problem in any Skribly tool, and how Skribly Agent, agent-skills and Skribly Tracker handle tokens, network access and your code.

## Report a vulnerability

[Section titled “Report a vulnerability”](#report-a-vulnerability)

Write to **<contact@skribly.pl>** with:

* the tool and version (in Skribly Agent: **Help → About**);
* what an attacker can do, and the steps to reproduce it;
* whether the problem is already public.

Please do not open a public issue or post details anywhere before we have answered. We will confirm that we received the report, keep you posted while we fix it, and credit you in the release notes if you want. Skribly is a spare-time, non-commercial project, so there is no bug bounty.

## Skribly Agent

[Section titled “Skribly Agent”](#skribly-agent)

* **No telemetry and no server of its own.** It sends no statistics, crash reports or identifiers.
* **Tokens in the system keychain.** Tracker tokens are encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows, libsecret on Linux). When encryption is not available, they stay in memory only and never reach disk in plain text.
* **An isolated interface.** Context isolation is on, the interface can call only the methods of one typed contract, and its Content-Security-Policy allows scripts from the app only. Embedded pages get no Node.js access.
* **Commands without a shell.** Git, agents and editors run through `execFile`, so arguments are never interpreted by a shell. File operations reject paths outside the project.
* **Local ports only.** The control API and the optional browser debugging port listen on `127.0.0.1` only. The control API needs a random token, renewed on every start.
* **Agents run with your permissions.** An agent in a terminal can do whatever you can do in a terminal, and it can read the tokens Skribly passes to its session. Run agents you trust.

Skribly Agent connects only to your trackers, `api.osv.dev` for dependency audits, `open-vsx.org` for themes, GitHub for updates and skills, the sites you audit or open, and a translation service when you choose a language other than Polish or English.

Caution

The browser debugging port, when you turn it on, can be used by **any program on your computer** without authentication, and it sees every tab, including signed-in ones. Turn it on only while agents need it.

## agent-skills

[Section titled “agent-skills”](#agent-skills)

* Credentials come from environment variables or `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env`, never from the repository. `agent-skills doctor` warns when others can read that file.
* The tracker client is read-only unless you publish a comment with `--post --yes`. Tokens are sent only to the tracker’s own host, and redirects to another host drop them.
* Secret scans mask the values they find.
* Nothing is collected or uploaded. The CLI talks only to your tracker, to OSV.dev or PageSpeed Insights when you run those audits, and to package registries through your own package manager.

## Skribly Tracker

[Section titled “Skribly Tracker”](#skribly-tracker)

* Personal access tokens act with their owner’s role and can be read-only or expire. See [Personal access tokens](/tracker/tokens/).
* Webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body. See [Webhooks and signing](/tracker/webhooks/).
* Markdown in descriptions and comments is rendered with raw HTML escaped.
* The API allows 240 requests a minute per user.
* When you host it yourself, put it behind HTTPS, set your own database passwords and an administrator password, and turn debugging off. See [Self-hosting](/tracker/self-hosting/#running-it-for-a-team).

## This site

[Section titled “This site”](#this-site)

docs.skribly.pl is a static site with no analytics, no tracking and no third-party requests: fonts and the search index are served from the same address. It keeps only your own display choices: the theme in the `sk-theme` cookie and the accessibility settings in the `sk-a11y` cookie, both on `.skribly.pl` so they hold on every Skribly site, plus a copy in the browser’s local storage. Neither is sent anywhere else.

# agent-skills

> 35 portable skills that take AI coding agents from a tracker ticket to a reviewed, tested commit - cheap on tokens, safe by default, with no AI co-author trailers.

**agent-skills** is a library of short, tested procedures (“skills”) for AI coding agents, plus a zero-dependency installer that puts them where each agent looks. It supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin.

Skills cover the whole loop: pick up a Redmine, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Linear or Skribly Tracker issue, plan, branch, implement in stages, test, review, audit and commit. They also cover the specialist jobs around it: Core Web Vitals, load tests, safe migrations, Docker, CI, dependency upgrades, translations and release notes. A group of skills also covers the work around the code: writing a plan as work packages and running a work package task by task, decision records, a release checklist, the check that docs and translations move with a change, and the design review of a page.

![The skills catalogue in Skribly Agent: cards for each skill with its command, group and the agents it is installed for](/_astro/skills-catalog.DRGjq_KS_Z1i9TlW.webp)

## Principles

[Section titled “Principles”](#principles)

* **Scripts do the mechanical work.** Small Node scripts hand the model a few lines instead of megabytes: a 455 KB Lighthouse report becomes 754 bytes, a 27 KB test log 86 bytes.
* **Every risky step waits for your OK.** Commits, comments on tracker issues, screenshots and long test runs are proposed, not done silently.
* **Adapts to each project.** The `project` skill detects the stack, the commands and the commit conventions into `.skribly/project.json`, and every skill reads that profile first. Values you set by hand are never overwritten.
* **Learns from the work.** At the end of `task`, `test-loop`, `review` and `debug` the agent proposes one confirmed lesson; with your OK, `learn` keeps it in `.skribly/lessons.md` for the next run. Lessons that look like secrets are refused.
* **Commits look like yours.** Messages follow the project’s convention, and no skill adds a `Co-Authored-By` or “Generated with” trailer.
* **Standalone.** It needs nothing else from Skribly and works in any repository. Skribly Agent is one optional place that uses it.

## Facts

[Section titled “Facts”](#facts)

|                      |                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Version              | 0.2.14 (11 November 2026)                                                                |
| Skills               | 35, in the shared [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification) format            |
| Agents               | 8: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Devin |
| Trackers             | Redmine, Jira Cloud and Server/Data Center, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Skribly Tracker      |
| Requirements         | `git` and Node.js 20 or newer                                                            |
| Runtime dependencies | None                                                                                     |
| Licence              | MIT                                                                                      |

## How a skill is built

[Section titled “How a skill is built”](#how-a-skill-is-built)

Every skill is a folder `skills/<name>/`:

```text
skills/<name>/
  SKILL.md       at most 110 lines, read when the skill runs
  reference/     extra detail, read only when a step needs it
  scripts/       Node scripts with no dependencies that do the mechanical work
  templates/     files the skill fills in
```

An agent keeps only each skill’s name and description in its context, one line per skill. The rest loads on demand.

## How it saves tokens

[Section titled “How it saves tokens”](#how-it-saves-tokens)

1. **Load on demand.** `SKILL.md` loads when used, `reference/` only when a step needs it. The 110-line limit is enforced in CI.

2. **Scripts instead of the model.** Measured on real projects:

   | Task                                    | Raw input     | Script output | Saved |
   | --------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- | ----- |
   | Lighthouse report                       | 455,534 bytes | 754 bytes     | 99.8% |
   | Test run log, 86 tests                  | 27,098 bytes  | 86 bytes      | 99.7% |
   | `npm audit --json` on a 300-package app | 20,555 bytes  | 2,126 bytes   | 90%   |
   | `git log -60` to learn the commit style | 7,415 bytes   | 739 bytes     | 90%   |
   | GitHub issue with comments              | 8,178 bytes   | 1,018 bytes   | 88%   |

3. **Ask before expensive steps.** Screenshots, Lighthouse runs and full suites need your OK.

4. **Restart instead of dragging transcripts.** `STATE.md` (about 30 lines) holds the goal, what was done and one next step, so you can `/clear` after each stage and resume, in the same or another agent.

5. **Working rules.** The `token-saver` skill gives every agent the same habits: search before reading, read line ranges, never open lock files or build output.

The full measurements are on [Token saving](/agent/token-saving/).

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Install](/skills/install/): user scope or project scope, updates, Windows.
* [Skills catalog](/skills/catalog/): every skill and when to use it.
* [Supported agents](/skills/agents/): where each agent gets the skills, and the files `agent-skills agent-files` generates from `AGENTS.md`.
* [Trackers](/skills/trackers/): credentials for each tracker.
* [Commits without AI trailers](/skills/commits/): the three layers that keep commits yours.

# Supported agents

> Where agent-skills installs skills for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin, and how you call them in each. Also the per-agent files that `agent-skills agent-files` generates from `AGENTS.md`.

Every supported agent reads native **Agent Skills** folders: `<name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` front matter, and optional `reference/`, `scripts/` and `templates/`. Seven of them read the same shared folder, `.agents/skills`, so one copy serves Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot and Devin. Claude Code reads only `.claude/skills`. Locations were checked against each vendor’s documentation on 29 October 2026, and those for Devin and for the project instruction files on 11 November 2026.

## Default format: `--format skills`

[Section titled “Default format: --format skills”](#default-format---format-skills)

| Agent          | Target     | Project scope (copy)                                       | User scope (symlink)                                                                                               | Invoke                                     |
| -------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Claude Code    | `claude`   | `.claude/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.claude/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `/task 123`                                |
| Codex CLI      | `codex`    | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `$task 123`, or pick from `/skills`        |
| Cursor         | `cursor`   | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `/task 123` in Agent chat                  |
| Gemini CLI     | `gemini`   | `.agents/skills/<name>/` + `.gemini/commands/<name>.toml`  | `~/.agents/skills/<name>` + `~/.gemini/commands/<name>.toml`                                                       | `/task 123`                                |
| OpenCode       | `opencode` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` + `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`  | `~/.agents/skills/<name>` + `~/.config/opencode/commands/<name>.md`                                                | `/task 123`                                |
| Windsurf       | `windsurf` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` + `.windsurf/workflows/<name>.md` | `~/.agents/skills/<name>` + `~/.codeium/windsurf/global_workflows/<name>.md`                                       | `/task 123` or `@task`                     |
| GitHub Copilot | `copilot`  | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`                                                                                          | `/task 123` in VS Code chat or Copilot CLI |
| Devin          | `devin`    | `.agents/skills/<name>/`                                   | `~/.agents/skills/<name>`; the Devin CLI also reads `~/.config/devin/skills` (on Windows `%APPDATA%\devin\skills`) | `@skills:task` in a prompt                 |

Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Windsurf load skills through a tool or an `@mention` rather than a slash command, so the installer also writes a thin command of a few lines: “use the `<name>` skill with these arguments”. It never duplicates the skill text, so `git pull` and `agent-skills sync` are enough to update.

## Classic format: `--format rules`

[Section titled “Classic format: --format rules”](#classic-format---format-rules)

For older agent versions:

| Target                     | Written                                                                              | Notes                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cursor`                   | `.cursor/rules/<name>.mdc` (“Agent Requested”)                                       | Project scope only                                                                           |
| `windsurf`                 | `.windsurf/rules/<name>.md` (`trigger: model_decision`)                              | Project scope only; the 12,000-character limit per file is checked                           |
| `copilot`                  | `.github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md`; user scope `~/.copilot/instructions/` | No `applyTo`, so it is not attached to every request                                         |
| `gemini`                   | `.gemini/commands/<name>.toml` with the whole skill inlined                          | `@{` and `!{` are neutralised so Gemini never injects files or runs commands from skill text |
| `opencode`                 | `.opencode/commands/<name>.md` with the whole skill inlined                          |                                                                                              |
| `claude`, `codex`, `devin` | Same as `skills`                                                                     | They have no other format                                                                    |

## Known overlaps

[Section titled “Known overlaps”](#known-overlaps)

* Cursor, OpenCode and Copilot also read `.claude/skills` at project scope. With Claude and one of those in the same project, a skill may show twice. Install Claude at user scope and the others at project scope, or the reverse.
* Codex still loads the deprecated `~/.codex/skills`. agent-skills never writes there, and `agent-skills doctor` warns when old copies shadow the new ones.

## Not fully verified

[Section titled “Not fully verified”](#not-fully-verified)

* **Windsurf** now prefers `.devin/{rules,workflows,skills}` and reads `.windsurf/*` as a fallback. agent-skills writes `.windsurf/*`, which works in both the old and the renamed app, and the shared `.agents/skills`.
* **Gemini CLI** restricts file tools to workspace folders. Skills linked at user scope are activated through `activate_skill`, which grants access to the skill folder.

## Project instruction files

[Section titled “Project instruction files”](#project-instruction-files)

A repository keeps its instructions for coding agents in one file, `AGENTS.md`. Codex, OpenCode and Devin read it themselves. Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Copilot need a small file of their own, and `agent-skills agent-files` generates those files from `AGENTS.md`, so you never write them by hand:

```bash
cd ~/code/shop                      # a repository with an AGENTS.md
agent-skills agent-files            # write what is missing or out of date
agent-skills agent-files --check    # write nothing, exit 1 when a generated file is missing or differs
agent-skills doctor                 # each agent: configured or not for this repository
```

Run it again after a `git pull` of agent-skills (new skill versions) or after a change to the structure of `AGENTS.md`. The pointer files contain no instructions, so editing `AGENTS.md` itself needs no re-run. The generator covers seven agents: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Devin. Windsurf reads `.agents/skills` and `AGENTS.md` too, so a generated repository works there without an extra file.

| File                              | For                                                                | Contents                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CLAUDE.md`                       | Claude Code                                                        | A marker comment, then the one line `@AGENTS.md`                    |
| `GEMINI.md`                       | Gemini CLI                                                         | A marker comment, then `@./AGENTS.md`                               |
