| `.cursor/rules/agents.mdc`        | Cursor                                                             | An always-applied rule that references `@AGENTS.md`                 |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | GitHub Copilot                                                     | A marker comment and a link to `../AGENTS.md`                       |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/`          | Claude Code                                                        | The skills, copied                                                  |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/`          | Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot, Devin (and Windsurf) | The same skills, once for all                                       |
| `.mcp.json`                       | Claude Code                                                        | `{ "mcpServers": {} }`: read-only defaults and an empty server list |
| `.skribly/agent-files.json`       | The command                                                        | What was generated; commit it with the other files                  |

Every text file starts with a comment that says it was generated by `agent-skills agent-files`. Claude Code strips that comment before it reads `CLAUDE.md`, so the agent still sees the single import line. `.mcp.json` never contains a token or a URL with credentials; servers are added by a person.

The command is safe to run again and again:

* **Twice is the same.** A second run changes nothing and prints `0 change(s)`; line endings do not matter.
* **Hand-written files are kept.** A `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, rule, instruction file or skill folder without the marker is reported and left alone, and the command exits 1. Move its content into `AGENTS.md` and delete it, or pass `--force`: the old file is saved as `<path>.bak-agent-skills` first.
* **Your own `.mcp.json` servers are kept.** `--force` leaves such a file alone; only `--force-mcp` replaces it, saving the old one as `.mcp.json.bak-agent-skills`. That backup may hold an `env` block with tokens, so delete it or ignore it before `git add`.
* **Your own skills are never touched.** Only folders named like an agent-skills skill are managed.
* **Everything stays inside the repository.** A link that points outside it is refused, reported and skipped; the command exits 1.
* **`--check` and `--dry-run` write nothing.** `--check` exits 1 when a generated file is missing, differs or has no marker, and is the gate to use in CI. `--skills a,b` limits which skills are copied, and `--json` prints a machine-readable report.

`agent-skills doctor` lists each of the seven agents as `configured` or `not configured` for the current repository, with the reason, for example `CLAUDE.md missing`. It reports; it does not change anything.

The generated files do not yet include the guard hook of each agent or the subagent roles of `.claude/agents/`.

## Agents in Skribly Agent

[Section titled “Agents in Skribly Agent”](#agents-in-skribly-agent)

Skribly Agent runs 13 agents, more than agent-skills supports. Aider, Amp, Factory Droid, Qwen Code, Goose, Crush and Kimi CLI run in Skribly but have no skill target. See [Supported agents in Skribly Agent](/agent/agents/).

# Skills catalog

> All 35 skills of agent-skills, grouped by job, with what each one does, when to use it and how to call it.

Invoke a skill as `/name` in Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf and Copilot, `$name` in Codex, or `@skills:name` in a Devin prompt. You can also just describe what you want: agents pick skills by their description.

The machine-readable list is `skills.json` in the repository, validated against a JSON schema in CI.

## Workflow

[Section titled “Workflow”](#workflow)

| Skill         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Example                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `task`        | Takes a ticket or a sentence to an approved commit: fetches the issue with a script, writes a small or large analysis (`SPEC.md` for approval), branches after approval, works in stages with `STATE.md` updated after each, runs the checks and commits after your OK. Extras: `estimate`, `plan`, `pr` (pull request description) and `comment` (tracker comment). | `/task 482` · `$task SHOP-42` · `/task fix the date sorting` · `/task` to resume the current branch’s task |
| `project`     | Detects the stack, the install, dev, build, test, lint, typecheck and format commands, the commit style and language, the base branch, CI and containers into `.skribly/project.json`, which every skill reads first. Values set by hand are never overwritten, and a value deleted by hand stays deleted.                                                           | `/project` · `$project` · “which commands does this repo use?”                                             |
| `commit`      | Proposes a message in the project’s convention, detected from your own recent commits, and commits the listed files after you approve. Never adds trailers, never pushes.                                                                                                                                                                                            | `/commit` · “commit this as two commits”                                                                   |
| `handoff`     | Writes or reads `.tasks/<id>/STATE.md` so another agent or a fresh session continues without the transcript.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `/handoff` · `$handoff resume 482`                                                                         |
| `orchestrate` | Splits big work into independent sub-tasks with self-contained briefs and file ownership, runs them in parallel subagents or worktrees, then merges and verifies.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `/orchestrate migrate all forms to the new validation helper`                                              |
| `estimate`    | A read-only estimate: deliverables, optimistic, likely and pessimistic hours, a PERT total and range, assumptions, risks and open questions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `/estimate 482`                                                                                            |
| `plan-step`   | Writes or expands a plan work package in the exact shape the plan defines: headings in order, tasks with their files, what to do and a check, owner actions, verification, done-when and risks. Task ids and section references stay stable. It writes a plan; it does not run a step.                                                                               | `/plan-step` · “write the work package for F9” · “add a task to F5”                                        |
| `run-step`    | Carries out one work package task by task by the plan’s step protocol: a short branch from `develop` for each task, its check, a Conventional Commit with explicit paths, a merge with `--no-ff`, a push, then the tick. Actions that belong to the owner are recorded as blocked, never attempted.                                                                  | `/run-step` · “run step F5” · “do the next task of F5”                                                     |
| `release`     | Walks the plan’s release checklist and runs read-only checks before a release: `develop` clean, `package.json` and `VERSION` in step, a `CHANGELOG.md` entry present, the tag still free. It never bumps a version, tags, merges into `main` or publishes.                                                                                                           | `/release` · “is this ready to release?” · “run the weekly routine”                                        |

## Quality and tests

[Section titled “Quality and tests”](#quality-and-tests)

| Skill           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Example                                            |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `test-loop`     | Runs only the checks affected by the change, fixes in a capped loop of three attempts, condenses logs, never weakens tests.                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/test-loop` · “make CI green”                     |
| `backend-tests` | Writes and runs backend tests for changed code: pytest with Django and DRF, Laravel PHPUnit or Pest, Node with supertest, Go, Spring. Test database, factories, isolation, mocked HTTP, coverage of changed lines.                                                                                                                        | `/backend-tests` · “cover the new orders endpoint” |
| `api-tests`     | Contract and integration tests for REST and GraphQL from OpenAPI (Schemathesis, Dredd, Hurl, newman), auth flows and error cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                         | “check the API against openapi.yaml”               |
| `e2e-tests`     | Playwright specs for changed user flows; runs only affected specs, keeps traces, fixes flaky tests at the root cause.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `/e2e-tests` · “this spec fails on CI only”        |
| `load-test`     | k6, autocannon or Locust from smoke to load, stress and spike, with thresholds and condensed results.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `/load-test GET /api/orders at 20 users`           |
| `review`        | Self-review of the diff before a commit: findings first, with severity, `file:line` and a fix.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `/review` · `/review src/billing`                  |
| `debug`         | Reproduce, narrow down, prove the cause, make the smallest fix, and use the same reproduction as proof.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `/debug totals are wrong after applying a coupon`  |
| `refactor`      | Behaviour-preserving refactoring: characterisation tests first, then small verified steps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `/refactor split OrderService`                     |
| `db-migrations` | Zero-downtime migrations for Django, Laravel, Prisma, Alembic, Flyway and Rails, with a linter for locks and risks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | “is this migration safe?”                          |
| `i18n`          | Missing, empty and unused translation keys, placeholder mismatches, keys used in code but missing, and string extraction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `/i18n` · “check the locale files”                 |
| `browser-check` | Headless Chromium screenshots of only the changed element, desktop and mobile, plus console errors. Only with your consent.                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/browser-check the cart badge on /cart`           |
| `design-review` | Reviews a page or component against the plan’s list of what fails a design review and its cross-site checklist. A script scans for emoji icons, gradients, glass effects, missing alt text, landmarks and heading, title, meta and hreflang rules; the rest is judged on screenshots at phone and desktop width in each theme. Read-only. | `/design-review` · “does this page fail review?”   |

[Section titled “Performance”](#performance)

| Skill          | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Example                                     |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `pagespeed`    | Core Web Vitals with PageSpeed Insights for public URLs or local Lighthouse for localhost, mobile and desktop, condensed to the top opportunities, with a fix-and-measure loop for Next.js, Vite, Django and Laravel. | `/pagespeed http://localhost:3000/products` |
| `perf-backend` | N+1 detection from query logs, indexes from `EXPLAIN`, caching and profiling, proven with before and after numbers.                                                                                                   | `/perf-backend /api/orders is slow`         |

[Section titled “Security and accessibility”](#security-and-accessibility)

| Skill            | What it does                                                                                                                                                   | Example                                      |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `security-audit` | A masked secret scan, vulnerable dependencies (npm, pnpm, Composer, pip or OSV.dev) and dangerous code patterns, with severity, evidence and fixes. Read-only. | `/security-audit` · `/security-audit full`   |
| `wcag-audit`     | WCAG 2.2 AA for the changed UI: axe-core through Playwright when available, plus a targeted checklist and concrete fixes.                                      | `/wcag-audit http://localhost:3000/checkout` |

## DevOps

[Section titled “DevOps”](#devops)

| Skill         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                    | Example                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `docker`      | Dockerfile and compose review and fixes: multi-stage builds, pinned images, non-root users, caching, healthchecks, secrets and exposed databases. Uses hadolint when installed. | `/docker` · “make the image smaller”       |
| `ci-setup`    | Creates or fixes GitHub Actions or GitLab CI for the detected stack, and reviews workflows for injection and unpinned actions. Uses actionlint when installed.                  | `/ci-setup` · “is our workflow safe?”      |
| `deps-update` | Outdated packages grouped by risk, changelogs read for majors, one group at a time with tests and a commit each.                                                                | `/deps-update` · “bump all patch versions” |

## Docs and meta

[Section titled “Docs and meta”](#docs-and-meta)

| Skill           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Example                                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `project-docs`  | A `.docs/` knowledge folder (overview, architecture, modules, data flow, development, decisions) and a short `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` that points to it.                                                                                                                                           | `/project-docs` · “slim down our CLAUDE.md”                      |
| `seo-audit`     | Technical SEO: meta tags, headings, canonical, robots and sitemap, hreflang, Open Graph, JSON-LD and performance basics.                                                                                                                                                                             | `/seo-audit https://example.com/product/1`                       |
| `release-notes` | Release notes and `CHANGELOG.md` entries from git history in the project’s style, without AI trailers.                                                                                                                                                                                               | `/release-notes since v1.4.0`                                    |
| `adr`           | Writes an architecture decision record in MADR 4.0.0 with the four fields Skribly requires (confidence, reopen when, exit plan and a confirmation that names its check), numbers it and keeps the index of `.docs/adr`. It refuses to edit an accepted record and supersedes it with a link instead. | `/adr` · “record this decision” · “supersede ADR 0007”           |
| `docs-sync`     | Checks that a change a user can see updated, in the same change, the Polish and English language files with the same keys, the repository’s `.docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the matching page on this site. Read-only: it reports what is missing and the agent adds it.                                | `/docs-sync` · “did I update the docs?”                          |
| `learn`         | Keeps confirmed project lessons (a command that works, a convention, a pitfall) in `.skribly/lessons.md`, one dated line each with the skill it came from, written only after you agree. Every skill reads the file first. Refuses anything that looks like a secret.                                | `/learn` · “remember that the e2e suite needs a seeded database” |
| `token-saver`   | Working rules for a small context: search before reading, line ranges, condensed logs, scripts instead of the model, `/clear` plus `STATE.md`.                                                                                                                                                       | `/token-saver` · “I’m close to the limit”                        |

## Files the skills leave behind

[Section titled “Files the skills leave behind”](#files-the-skills-leave-behind)

| File                             | Written by                             | What it holds                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.skribly/project.json`          | `project`, project-scope installs, you | The project profile: stack, commands, commit style and language, base branch and, optionally, the Skribly Tracker project. Its schema comes from [`@skribly/core`](/core/) |
| `.skribly/project.detected.json` | `project`                              | The last detection, so the next run can tell detected values from values you set by hand                                                                                   |
| `.skribly/lessons.md`            | `learn`, after your OK                 | Dated one-line lessons, each with the skill it came from                                                                                                                   |
| `.tasks/<id>/TASK.md`            | `task`                                 | The issue as fetched, refreshed with only the changes on later fetches                                                                                                     |
| `.tasks/<id>/SPEC.md`            | `task`                                 | The analysis of a larger task, for your approval                                                                                                                           |
| `.tasks/<id>/STATE.md`           | `task`, `handoff`                      | About 30 lines: goal, what is done, changed files, check results, decisions, one next step                                                                                 |
| `.tasks/<id>/COMMENT.md`         | `task`                                 | A draft tracker comment, posted only after your explicit OK                                                                                                                |
| `.tasks/workflow.md`             | `task`                                 | Project conventions: tracker, base branch, branch and commit patterns, check commands, dev URL                                                                             |

`.tasks/` is added to `.git/info/exclude`, so fetched tickets never land in a commit and the team’s `.gitignore` stays untouched. The `.skribly/` files are meant to be committed with the project, so the whole team and every agent read the same profile and lessons.

# Commits without AI trailers

> The three independent layers agent-skills uses so commits look like yours - the skills themselves, the Claude Code attribution setting and a commit-msg hook for any tool.

Commits should look like yours. agent-skills uses three independent layers, so one failing does not matter.

## 1. The skills

[Section titled “1. The skills”](#1-the-skills)

`commit` and `task` write messages in the project’s convention, from `.tasks/workflow.md` or detected from your own recent commits, and never add trailers: no `Co-Authored-By`, no “Generated with”, no agent links or emoji signatures. They commit only after you say OK, stage only the listed files, and never push, merge, rebase or force unless you ask in that conversation.

## 2. The Claude Code setting

[Section titled “2. The Claude Code setting”](#2-the-claude-code-setting)

```bash
agent-skills config attribution off                # ~/.claude/settings.json
agent-skills config attribution off --project .    # this project's .claude/settings.json
agent-skills config attribution status
agent-skills config attribution on                 # undo
```

It sets `"attribution": { "commit": "", "pr": "" }`, which hides the commit trailer and the pull request footer, and the older `"includeCoAuthoredBy": false` for earlier Claude Code versions. Other keys are kept, a backup is written before the first change, and invalid JSON is never overwritten.

## 3. The git hook, for any tool

[Section titled “3. The git hook, for any tool”](#3-the-git-hook-for-any-tool)

```bash
cd ~/code/shop
agent-skills hooks install
agent-skills hooks status
agent-skills hooks uninstall
```

The `commit-msg` hook removes:

* `Co-authored-by:` trailers. All of them by default; to keep human co-authors, run `git config agent-skills.keepHumanCoauthors true`, and only AI ones are removed.
* Footers such as “Generated with Claude Code”, “Generated by GitHub Copilot” or “Made with Cursor”. A “generated, made or created with” line is removed only when it names an AI tool, so “Generated with protoc” stays.

It never touches anything else: the subject, the body, `Signed-off-by`, comment lines and everything below the scissors line of `git commit -v` stay byte for byte, line endings included.

* Your existing `commit-msg` hook is kept and still runs after this one; uninstalling restores it.
* In repositories that use husky, lefthook or another `core.hooksPath`, the installer does not take over that folder. It prints one line to add to your own hook: `node .git/hooks/agent-skills-commit-msg.cjs "$1"`.
* The hook needs `node` on `PATH`; without it, the hook skips itself instead of blocking commits.
* Hooks are per repository and are not committed. Install it in each clone.

Skribly Agent has the same hook built in: **Code & git → Hook without AI trailers**.

## Checking old commits

[Section titled “Checking old commits”](#checking-old-commits)

```bash
git log --format='%h %s%n%b' | grep -inE 'co-authored-by|generated with' | head
```

Rewriting published history is a team decision; agent-skills never does it.

# Install agent-skills

> Install agent-skills for one or all eight agents, at user or project scope, keep it updated and remove it cleanly.

## Requirements

[Section titled “Requirements”](#requirements)

* `git` and **Node.js 20 or newer** (`node --version`). No npm packages are installed: the CLI and every skill script use only Node’s standard library.
* At least one supported agent: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot or Devin.

Access

The repository is private for now, so cloning needs access to the Skribly organisation on GitHub.

## Install in a minute

[Section titled “Install in a minute”](#install-in-a-minute)

1. Clone the repository and put the command on your `PATH`:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/skribly/agent-skills.git ~/agent-skills
   cd ~/agent-skills
   npm link
   ```

2. Install every skill for every agent, at user scope:

   ```bash
   agent-skills install --target all
   ```

3. Turn off Claude Code’s own attribution and check the result:

   ```bash
   agent-skills config attribution off
   agent-skills doctor
   ```

4. Restart your agent, or open a new chat, so it reads its skills folder again. Then try `/task 123` in Claude Code or `$task 123` in Codex.

On Windows use the same commands in PowerShell with `$HOME\agent-skills`. Folder links are created as junctions, which need no administrator rights. Without `npm link`, run `node cli/agent-skills.mjs …` or `bin\agent-skills.cmd …`.

## User scope or project scope

[Section titled “User scope or project scope”](#user-scope-or-project-scope)

|          | User scope (default)                      | Project scope                                             |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Command  | `agent-skills install --target all`       | `agent-skills install --target all --project ~/code/shop` |
| Where    | `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, … | `<project>/.claude/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, … |
| How      | Symlinks to the repository                | Copies                                                    |
| Updates  | `git pull`, then `agent-skills sync`      | `agent-skills sync` after `git pull`                      |
| Good for | Your own machine, all projects            | Sharing with a team through the project’s repository      |

A project-scope install also detects the project profile, `.skribly/project.json`; pass `--no-detect` to skip it.

You can mix them: install everything at user scope and commit `task` and `commit` into a team project so colleagues get them too. Choose explicitly with `--scope user|project`, `--link` or `--copy`.

## Choose skills and agents

[Section titled “Choose skills and agents”](#choose-skills-and-agents)

```bash
agent-skills install --target claude,codex --skills task,commit,handoff,review,test-loop,token-saver
agent-skills list
```

`--target` takes `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `windsurf`, `copilot`, `devin` or `all`. `--format rules` writes the classic formats for older agent versions; see [Supported agents](/skills/agents/).

## Recommended setup

[Section titled “Recommended setup”](#recommended-setup)

```bash
agent-skills config attribution off             # Claude Code: no Co-Authored-By trailer or PR footer
cd ~/code/shop && agent-skills hooks install    # per repository: strip AI trailers from any tool
```

Then configure your tracker as in [Trackers](/skills/trackers/).

## Connect a tracker

[Section titled “Connect a tracker”](#connect-a-tracker)

```bash
agent-skills tasks check
agent-skills tasks list
agent-skills tasks fetch 482
```

Credentials come from environment variables or `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env`, never from the repository. The first fetch writes `.tasks/<id>/TASK.md`, later fetches print only what changed, and `.tasks/` is excluded locally, so fetched tickets stay out of commits.

## Update and remove

[Section titled “Update and remove”](#update-and-remove)

```bash
cd ~/agent-skills && git pull && agent-skills sync      # refresh everything that was installed
agent-skills uninstall --target all                     # user scope
agent-skills uninstall --target all --project ~/code/shop
```

Installs are recorded in `~/.config/agent-skills/installs.json` with a hash of each file. `uninstall` removes only what agent-skills installed, keeps files you edited unless you pass `--force`, and deletes folders it leaves empty. A file agent-skills did not write is never overwritten; with `--force` it is moved to `<path>.bak-agent-skills` first.

## CLI reference

[Section titled “CLI reference”](#cli-reference)

| Command                                                                                                                                                                | Purpose                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent-skills list [--json]`                                                                                                                                           | The catalogue                                                                                                                                 |
| `agent-skills install --target <agents\|all> [--scope user\|project] [--project <dir>] [--skills a,b] [--link\|--copy] [--format skills\|rules] [--dry-run] [--force]` | Install                                                                                                                                       |
| `agent-skills uninstall --target … [--scope] [--project] [--skills]`                                                                                                   | Remove only what was installed                                                                                                                |
| `agent-skills sync`                                                                                                                                                    | Re-apply every recorded install after `git pull`                                                                                              |
| `agent-skills project [--project <dir>] [--dry-run] [--json]`                                                                                                          | Detect the project into `.skribly/project.json`, keeping values set by hand                                                                   |
| `agent-skills agent-files [--project <dir>] [--check] [--force] [--force-mcp] [--skills a,b\|all] [--dry-run] [--json]`                                                | Generate the per-agent files of a repository from its `AGENTS.md`; see [Project instruction files](/skills/agents/#project-instruction-files) |
| `agent-skills doctor [--project <dir>] [--json]`                                                                                                                       | Agents, installs, trackers, hook, attribution and whether each agent is configured for the repository                                         |
| `agent-skills hooks install\|uninstall\|status [--project <dir>]`                                                                                                      | The `commit-msg` hook                                                                                                                         |
| `agent-skills config attribution off\|on\|status [--project <dir>]`                                                                                                    | Claude Code attribution                                                                                                                       |
| `agent-skills tasks fetch\|attachments\|list\|comment-draft\|event\|detect\|check`                                                                                     | The tracker client; `event` prints the `skills.task.completed` event of a task                                                                |
| `agent-skills manifest [--check\|--write]`                                                                                                                             | Validate skills, sync shared files, regenerate `skills.json`                                                                                  |

## With Skribly Agent

[Section titled “With Skribly Agent”](#with-skribly-agent)

[Skribly Agent](/agent/features/#skills) clones agent-skills, shows the catalogue from `skills.json` (a stable v1 contract with a JSON schema), installs the chosen skills per project and per agent through this CLI, and can ask an agent to adapt them to the project. It runs the CLI with its own runtime, so no separate Node.js is needed there.

# Trackers

> Connect agent-skills to Redmine, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Linear or Skribly Tracker, and use the tasks commands that the task skill runs.

The `task` skill fetches issues with a script (`agent-skills tasks`), so the model spends no tokens on HTTP, pagination or re-reading. The first fetch writes `.tasks/<id>/TASK.md`; later fetches print only what changed: new comments, status, a changed description, new attachments.

## Credentials

[Section titled “Credentials”](#credentials)

Put them in environment variables or in `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\agent-skills\credentials.env`). Environment variables win over the file. Start from the template in the repository:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/agent-skills
cp templates/credentials.env.example ~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env
chmod 600 ~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env     # doctor warns if others can read it
agent-skills tasks check                             # who am I, per configured tracker
```

Never put tokens in a repository, in `.tasks/` or in a chat. Point at another file with `AGENT_SKILLS_CREDENTIALS`. Inside [Skribly Agent](/agent/features/#tasks-and-trackers), sessions receive these variables from the app, so no file is needed.

## Skribly Tracker

[Section titled “Skribly Tracker”](#skribly-tracker)

```bash
SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL=http://localhost:8100   # base URL of the instance
SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN=...                   # Profile -> API tokens
```

Ids: `ABC-12` or an `/issues/ABC-12` URL on the `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL` host. The client uses [REST API v1](/tracker/rest-api/); descriptions and comments are already Markdown, and attachments are downloaded with the same token. “My open tasks” is `assignee=me&status=open&sort=-updated`.

Older setups keep working: `skryba` is an alias of the `skribly` tracker id, and `SKRYBA_TRACKER_URL` and `SKRYBA_TRACKER_TOKEN` are read when the matching `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_*` variable is not set.

## Redmine

[Section titled “Redmine”](#redmine)

```bash
REDMINE_URL=https://redmine.example.com
REDMINE_API_KEY=...        # My account -> API access key (an admin must enable the REST API)
```

Ids: `123`, `#123` or an `/issues/123` URL. Comments are journal notes.

## Jira Cloud

[Section titled “Jira Cloud”](#jira-cloud)

```bash
JIRA_URL=https://your-team.atlassian.net
JIRA_EMAIL=you@example.com
JIRA_API_TOKEN=...         # id.atlassian.com -> Security -> API tokens
```

## Jira Server / Data Center

[Section titled “Jira Server / Data Center”](#jira-server--data-center)

```bash
JIRA_URL=https://jira.example.com
JIRA_PAT=...               # Profile -> Personal Access Tokens
```

Ids: `ABC-123` or a `/browse/ABC-123` URL. Wiki markup is converted to Markdown.

## GitHub

[Section titled “GitHub”](#github)

```bash
GITHUB_TOKEN=...           # fine-grained token: Issues read (write only to post comments)
GITHUB_API_URL=https://github.example.com/api/v3   # GitHub Enterprise Server only
```

Without a token, a signed-in GitHub CLI (`gh auth login`) is used, and public issues work anonymously at 60 requests an hour. Ids: `7` (the repository of the `origin` remote), `owner/repo#7` or an issue URL.

## GitLab

[Section titled “GitLab”](#gitlab)

```bash
GITLAB_TOKEN=...           # read_api (api to post comments)
GITLAB_URL=https://gitlab.example.com   # default https://gitlab.com
```

Ids: `7`, `group/sub/project#7` or a `/-/issues/7` URL. System notes are skipped.

## Linear

[Section titled “Linear”](#linear)

```bash
LINEAR_API_KEY=lin_api_...  # Settings -> Security & access -> Personal API keys
```

Ids: `ENG-12` or a `linear.app/.../issue/ENG-12/...` URL.

## Which tracker does an id mean?

[Section titled “Which tracker does an id mean?”](#which-tracker-does-an-id-mean)

In order: `--tracker`, the `Tracker:` line in `.tasks/workflow.md`, `AGENT_SKILLS_TRACKER`, then whichever tracker is configured. A configured Redmine wins for plain numbers; GitHub or GitLab when the `origin` remote points there. `ABC-12` can be Jira, Linear or Skribly Tracker: the same three settings decide, otherwise the only configured one is used, and with several you are asked. A task fetched once remembers its tracker.

## Commands

[Section titled “Commands”](#commands)

```bash
agent-skills tasks fetch 123                 # TASK.md; on re-fetch only the changes
agent-skills tasks attachments 123 [name]    # images by default, --all for every file
agent-skills tasks list                      # my open issues in every configured tracker (--json)
agent-skills tasks list --local              # tasks in .tasks/ with status, branch and next step
agent-skills tasks comment-draft 123         # create or show .tasks/123/COMMENT.md
agent-skills tasks comment-draft 123 --post --yes    # publish, only after your explicit OK
agent-skills tasks detect                    # git facts used to write .tasks/workflow.md
agent-skills tasks check                     # configuration and token test
```

## Safety

[Section titled “Safety”](#safety)

* Read-only by default. Writing needs `--post --yes`, and the same text is never posted twice.
* Tokens are sent only to the tracker’s own host. Redirects to another host, such as a CDN serving an attachment, are followed without credentials.
* Behind a corporate proxy with TLS errors, point `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` at the proxy’s CA certificate.

# Troubleshooting agent-skills

> Fixes for common agent-skills problems - agents that do not see skills, install conflicts, Windows links, tracker errors, the commit hook and optional tools.

## The agent does not see the skills

[Section titled “The agent does not see the skills”](#the-agent-does-not-see-the-skills)

* Run `agent-skills doctor`: it shows which agents were detected and where skills are installed.
* Restart the agent or start a new chat; most agents scan skill folders at startup.
* Check the location for your agent in [Supported agents](/skills/agents/). Older versions may need `--format rules`.
* Codex lists a skill twice: old copies sit in the deprecated `~/.codex/skills`. `doctor` warns about them; remove them.
* Cursor, OpenCode or Copilot list a skill twice in a project: they also read `.claude/skills`. Install Claude at user scope and the others at project scope, or the reverse.

## `agent-skills: command not found`

[Section titled “agent-skills: command not found”](#agent-skills-command-not-found)

Run `npm link` in the repository, call `node ~/agent-skills/cli/agent-skills.mjs`, or link `bin/agent-skills` into a folder on `PATH` (`ln -s ~/agent-skills/bin/agent-skills ~/.local/bin/`). On Windows use `bin\agent-skills.cmd`.

## “exists and was not installed by agent-skills”

[Section titled ““exists and was not installed by agent-skills””](#exists-and-was-not-installed-by-agent-skills)

A file or folder with the same name was already there, so it was left alone. Compare it, then rerun with `--force`; the old one is moved to `<path>.bak-agent-skills`.

## `sync` or `uninstall` skips a copy I edited

[Section titled “sync or uninstall skips a copy I edited”](#sync-or-uninstall-skips-a-copy-i-edited)

On purpose: hand-edited copies are never overwritten or deleted. Keep your edit, or use `--force` to replace or remove it.

## Links on Windows

[Section titled “Links on Windows”](#links-on-windows)

User-scope installs create folder junctions, which need no administrator rights or developer mode. If a junction cannot be created, for example on some network drives, install with `--copy` and run `agent-skills sync` after updates.

## WSL and Windows at the same time

[Section titled “WSL and Windows at the same time”](#wsl-and-windows-at-the-same-time)

Each environment has its own home folder and agents. Install in both, from one clone if you like, running `agent-skills install` inside each environment.

## Tracker problems

[Section titled “Tracker problems”](#tracker-problems)

* `access denied (HTTP 401/403)`: a wrong or expired token, or a missing scope. `agent-skills tasks check` tests every tracker.
* `cannot resolve` or `no connection`: VPN or URL. `TLS problem`: set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to your company’s CA certificate.
* `ENG-12 could be Jira or Linear` (or Skribly Tracker): add `Tracker: jira` (or `linear`, `skribly`) to `.tasks/workflow.md`, set `AGENT_SKILLS_TRACKER`, or pass `--tracker`.
* GitHub without a token: public issues work at 60 requests an hour; private ones need `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth login`.

## PageSpeed Insights says HTTP 429

[Section titled “PageSpeed Insights says HTTP 429”](#pagespeed-insights-says-http-429)

The keyless quota is shared and often used up. Create an API key for the PageSpeed Insights API and set `PSI_API_KEY`, or measure locally with `--local`, which needs Chrome.

## Playwright or axe-core is missing

[Section titled “Playwright or axe-core is missing”](#playwright-or-axe-core-is-missing)

`browser-check`, `wcag-audit` and `e2e-tests` look for Playwright in the project, then globally. Install it only if you want it: `npm i -D playwright axe-core && npx playwright install chromium`. Without it the skills fall back to manual checklists and say so.

## The commit-msg hook did not run

[Section titled “The commit-msg hook did not run”](#the-commit-msg-hook-did-not-run)

* Run `agent-skills hooks status` in that repository. Hooks are per repository.
* husky, lefthook and similar tools set `core.hooksPath`; add the printed line to their `commit-msg` hook.
* `node` must be on `PATH` for git. GUI clients sometimes have a minimal `PATH`.

## Does it send my code anywhere?

[Section titled “Does it send my code anywhere?”](#does-it-send-my-code-anywhere)

No. The CLI talks only to your tracker (when you fetch, or explicitly post), to OSV.dev or PageSpeed Insights when you run those audits, and to package registries through your own package manager. Nothing else is collected or uploaded.

## How do I use it in a team?

[Section titled “How do I use it in a team?”](#how-do-i-use-it-in-a-team)

Install at project scope (`--project .`) and commit `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, so everyone gets the same skills. `.tasks/` stays personal. Put shared conventions (base branch, commit pattern, check commands) in `AGENTS.md`, and each developer’s `.tasks/workflow.md` is proposed from them. Each developer installs the commit hook in their own clone.

# Skribly Tracker

> The issue tracker of the Skribly ecosystem - workspaces, projects, issues, workflows, roles, boards, comments and time logs, with a REST API designed for coding agents.

**Skribly Tracker** plans the work that the rest of Skribly carries out: projects, issues with keys like `AGENT-12`, Kanban boards, comments and time logs. It runs in the browser, and its REST API is designed for coding agents as much as for people.

![The Kanban board of a sample project with four columns: To do, In progress, Review and Done](/_astro/tracker-board.ByjEJGOM_Z1Ji1yG.webp)

Status

First release, 0.1. The browser interface, the REST API v1 with personal access tokens, signed webhooks, the Docker stack and the agent-skills `skribly` tracker work today. The released version runs on PHP 8.4 and Laravel 12 with MySQL 8.4; moving it to the shared Node.js stack is planned and would keep the same API.

## Concepts

[Section titled “Concepts”](#concepts)

| Concept             | What it is                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Workspace**       | The top level that holds projects and people                                                                                                                                           |
| **Project**         | A set of issues with a short key such as `AGENT` or `WEB`, its own workflow, labels and members                                                                                        |
| **Issue**           | A unit of work with a key made of the project key and a number, like `AGENT-12`. It has a type, status, priority, labels, assignee, reporter, estimate, due date, parent and subtasks. |
| **Issue type**      | `task`, `bug` or `feature`                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Priority**        | `lowest`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `urgent`                                                                                                                                          |
| **Status**          | A column of the project’s workflow. *To do, In progress, Review, Done* by default.                                                                                                     |
| **Status category** | Each status belongs to `todo`, `in_progress` or `done`. “Open” means not done.                                                                                                         |
| **Comment**         | Markdown text on an issue                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Time entry**      | Hours logged on an issue with a date, a comment and an activity: `development`, `review`, `testing`, `design`, `meeting` or `other`                                                    |
| **Watcher**         | A person who follows an issue without being assigned                                                                                                                                   |
| **Attachment**      | A file on an issue, up to 10 MB by default                                                                                                                                             |
| **Activity log**    | Every change to an issue, with who made it and when                                                                                                                                    |

## Workflow

[Section titled “Workflow”](#workflow)

Each project has its own workflow in **Project → Settings → Workflow**. Admins can rename, reorder and add statuses, and give each one a category. Any status of the issue’s project can be set; there are no fixed transitions.

## Roles

[Section titled “Roles”](#roles)

| Role       | What it can do                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Admin**  | Everything, plus projects, workflows, people and webhooks                 |
| **Member** | Create and work on issues: edit, comment, assign, change status, log time |
| **Viewer** | Read only                                                                 |

API tokens act with their owner’s role, and can be made read-only on top of it. See [Personal access tokens](/tracker/tokens/).

## Views

[Section titled “Views”](#views)

| View          | What it shows                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Dashboard** | Your open issues, watched issues, projects and recent activity                                                                               |
| **Board**     | A Kanban board with drag and drop between the columns of the project’s workflow. With a keyboard, open an issue and change its status there. |
| **List**      | Filters, search and sorting, shared with the API                                                                                             |
| **Issue**     | Markdown description, subtasks, comments, time log, attachments and history                                                                  |
| **Profile**   | Language, theme and API tokens                                                                                                               |

The interface is in Polish and English, with light and dark themes that follow the system and switch from the top bar, and an accessibility panel on every page for text size, contrast, fonts and motion. WCAG 2.2 AA is the target.

## Connect the other tools

[Section titled “Connect the other tools”](#connect-the-other-tools)

### Skribly Agent

[Section titled “Skribly Agent”](#skribly-agent)

Skribly Tracker is the default tracker of Skribly Agent. Add a Skribly Tracker account with the address and a read-write token. Tasks assigned to you appear in the app, which can comment, change status, assign and log time. See [Personal access tokens](/tracker/tokens/).

### agent-skills

[Section titled “agent-skills”](#agent-skills)

The `task` skill reads this tracker like any other. Put the address and token in `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env`:

```bash
SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL=http://localhost:8100
SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN=...
```

Then run `agent-skills tasks check`, and `/task AGENT-12` in your agent. See [Trackers](/skills/trackers/#skribly-tracker).

## Built for agents

[Section titled “Built for agents”](#built-for-agents)

* The REST API maps one call to one method of Skribly Agent’s tracker client, and to the agent-skills `task` skill. See the [mapping](/tracker/rest-api/#skribly-agent-mapping).
* Issue keys are case-insensitive and a leading `#` is ignored, so an agent can paste what it reads.
* Descriptions and comments are Markdown, returned exactly as written.
* `updated_since` lets a client poll for changes cheaply.
* Signed [webhooks](/tracker/webhooks/) tell any service when issues change.

## Read next

[Section titled “Read next”](#read-next)

* [Self-hosting with Docker](/tracker/self-hosting/)
* [Configuration](/tracker/configuration/)
* [Personal access tokens](/tracker/tokens/)
* [REST API guide](/tracker/rest-api/) and the generated [API reference](/tracker/api/)
* [Webhooks and signing](/tracker/webhooks/)

# Configuration

> The environment variables that configure Skribly Tracker - application, database, queue, mail and the Tracker's own limits.

Skribly Tracker reads its settings from `.env`. Start from `.env.example`. In Docker Compose, the stack sets the database host and the queue itself, so you rarely need more than the variables marked below.

## Tracker

[Section titled “Tracker”](#tracker)

| Variable                  | Default | What it does                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TRACKER_PORT`            | `8100`  | Host port of the nginx container                                                          |
| `TRACKER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`  | empty   | Password of the administrator account the seeder creates. Required for a production seed. |
| `TRACKER_MAX_UPLOAD_KB`   | `10240` | Largest attachment, in kilobytes                                                          |
| `TRACKER_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT` | `5`     | Seconds a webhook delivery may take before it is abandoned                                |
| `TRACKER_VERSION`         | `0.1.0` | Version shown in the interface and in the webhook `User-Agent`                            |

## Application

[Section titled “Application”](#application)

| Variable              | Default                 | What it does                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `APP_NAME`            | `Skribly Tracker`       | Name in the interface and in e-mails                                                               |
| `APP_ENV`             | `local`                 | `production` for a real install; also decides whether development packages are installed in Docker |
| `APP_KEY`             | empty                   | Encryption key; the entrypoint generates it on first boot                                          |
| `APP_DEBUG`           | `true`                  | Set to `false` in production                                                                       |
| `APP_URL`             | `http://localhost:8100` | Public address; used in issue and attachment URLs in the API                                       |
| `APP_TIMEZONE`        | `Europe/Warsaw`         | Time zone of timestamps in the API and webhooks                                                    |
| `APP_LOCALE`          | `en`                    | Default interface language, `en` or `pl`; people choose their own on the profile page              |
| `APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE` | `en`                    | Language used when a translation is missing                                                        |

## Database

[Section titled “Database”](#database)

| Variable                                              | Default             | What it does                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DB_CONNECTION`                                       | `mysql`             | `mysql` or `sqlite`                                                                        |
| `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`                                  | `127.0.0.1`, `3306` | Docker Compose sets the host to `mysql`                                                    |
| `DB_DATABASE`                                         | `skryba_tracker`    | The database name keeps the former product name, so existing data directories keep working |
| `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD`                          | example values      | Change them for any shared install                                                         |
| `MYSQL_USER`, `MYSQL_PASSWORD`, `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` | example values      | Used by the MySQL container on its first start                                             |

## Queue, cache, sessions and logs

[Section titled “Queue, cache, sessions and logs”](#queue-cache-sessions-and-logs)

| Variable           | Default    | What it does                                          |
| ------------------ | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `QUEUE_CONNECTION` | `database` | Webhook deliveries are queued jobs; a worker must run |
| `CACHE_STORE`      | `file`     |                                                       |
| `SESSION_DRIVER`   | `file`     |                                                       |
| `SESSION_LIFETIME` | `120`      | Minutes until a browser session expires               |
| `LOG_CHANNEL`      | `stack`    | Docker Compose logs to `stderr`                       |
| `LOG_LEVEL`        | `debug`    | Use `warning` or higher in production                 |

## Mail

[Section titled “Mail”](#mail)

| Variable            | Default              | What it does                                                 |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `MAIL_MAILER`       | `log`                | Mail is written to the log until you configure a real mailer |
| `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` | `tracker@skribly.pl` | Sender address; set your own                                 |
| `MAIL_FROM_NAME`    | `${APP_NAME}`        | Sender name                                                  |

## Development

[Section titled “Development”](#development)

| Variable           | What it does                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `VITE_DEV_SERVER`  | `true` serves assets from the Vite container with hot reload                                                 |
| `DB_WAIT_ATTEMPTS` | How many times the entrypoint retries the database at two-second intervals before giving up; `60` by default |

## Clients

[Section titled “Clients”](#clients)

Clients of the Tracker read two variables of their own. Skribly Agent passes them to every agent session, and agent-skills reads them from the environment or its credentials file:

| Variable                | Example                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL`   | `http://localhost:8100`                     |
| `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN` | A [personal access token](/tracker/tokens/) |

The former names `SKRYBA_TRACKER_URL` and `SKRYBA_TRACKER_TOKEN` keep working as fallbacks.

# REST API guide

> How to use the Skribly Tracker REST API v1 - authentication, conventions, the issue object, filters, curl examples for every common task, and the mapping to Skribly Agent's tracker client.

The base URL is `http://localhost:8100/api/v1` on the Docker stack; every path below is relative to it. JSON in, JSON out. Every operation, parameter and schema is in the generated [API reference](/tracker/api/), built from the OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API.

```bash
export TRACKER=http://localhost:8100/api/v1
export TOKEN='1|…'
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/json" "$TRACKER/me"
```

Create the token as described in [Personal access tokens](/tracker/tokens/).

## Authentication

[Section titled “Authentication”](#authentication)

Create a personal access token in your profile and send it as a bearer token. A token acts with its owner’s role: viewers can only read, members and admins can change issues, and webhooks are for admins. Endpoints that change data also need the token’s `write` ability.

## Conventions

[Section titled “Conventions”](#conventions)

* **Issue keys** look like `WEB-12`. They are case-insensitive, a leading `#` is ignored, and the numeric `id` works too.
* **Options** are objects `{ "id": "…", "name": "…" }`: `type` (`task`, `bug`, `feature`), `priority` (`lowest`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`) and time `activity` (`development`, `review`, `testing`, `design`, `meeting`, `other`). Status ids are numbers, sent as strings in `transitions`; a status may also be given by name, like `"Review"`.
* **Status category** is `todo`, `in_progress` or `done`. `status=open` means “not done”.
* **Markdown**: `description` and comment `body` are Markdown, returned as written. The web interface renders them with raw HTML escaped.
* **Dates**: ISO 8601 with an offset for timestamps; `YYYY-MM-DD` for `due_date` and the `date` of a time entry.
* **Pagination**: list endpoints return `data`, `links` and `meta { current_page, last_page, per_page, total }`. `per_page` is 1-100 (25 by default), `page` starts at 1.
* **Rate limit**: 240 requests a minute per user.

## Errors

[Section titled “Errors”](#errors)

```json
{ "message": "The title field is required.", "errors": { "title": ["The title field is required."] } }
```

| Status | Meaning                                                   |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `401`  | No token, or a bad, revoked or expired one                |
| `403`  | The owner’s role or the token’s ability does not allow it |
| `404`  | No such issue, project or resource                        |
| `422`  | Validation failed; `errors` names the fields              |
| `429`  | More than 240 requests a minute                           |

## The issue object

[Section titled “The issue object”](#the-issue-object)

```json
{
  "id": 13,
  "key": "AGENT-1",
  "number": 1,
  "title": "Skribly Tracker as the default tracker",
  "description": "Add a `skribly` TrackerClient…",
  "type": { "id": "feature", "name": "Feature" },
  "status": { "id": 6, "name": "In progress", "category": "in_progress" },
  "priority": { "id": "urgent", "name": "Urgent" },
  "labels": ["trackers"],
  "assignee": { "id": 1, "name": "Ada Example", "email": "ada@example.com" },
  "reporter": { "id": 1, "name": "Ada Example", "email": "ada@example.com" },
  "project": { "id": 2, "key": "AGENT", "name": "Skribly Agent" },
  "parent": null,
  "subtasks": [{ "key": "AGENT-4", "title": "…", "status": "To do" }],
  "estimate_hours": 8,
  "spent_hours": 1.5,
  "due_date": "2026-11-03",
  "url": "http://localhost:8100/issues/AGENT-1",
  "created_at": "2026-10-03T09:12:00+01:00",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-29T20:10:36+01:00",
  "closed_at": null,
  "comments": [
    { "id": 6, "author": { "id": 5, "name": "Skribly Agent" }, "body": "Started on the adapter.",
      "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…" }
  ],
  "attachments": [
    { "id": 3, "name": "screen.png", "size": 48213, "type": "image/png",
      "url": "http://localhost:8100/api/v1/attachments/3" }
  ]
}
```

`comments` and `attachments` come only with `GET /issues/{key}`. `labels` are names. Attachment URLs need the same bearer token.

## Endpoints

[Section titled “Endpoints”](#endpoints)

| Method    | Path                         | Purpose                                                   |
| --------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET       | `/me`                        | The token’s owner and abilities                           |
| GET       | `/users`                     | People an issue can be assigned to                        |
| GET       | `/projects`                  | Active projects with `open_issues`                        |
| GET       | `/projects/{key}`            | A project with its statuses, labels, types and priorities |
| GET       | `/projects/{key}/meta`       | What can be chosen when creating an issue                 |
| GET       | `/issues`                    | A filtered, paginated list                                |
| POST      | `/issues`                    | Create (write)                                            |
| GET       | `/issues/{key}`              | One issue with comments and attachments                   |
| PATCH     | `/issues/{key}`              | Change some fields (write)                                |
| DELETE    | `/issues/{key}`              | Delete (admin or reporter; write)                         |
| GET       | `/issues/{key}/transitions`  | The statuses of its project, with `current` marked        |
| POST      | `/issues/{key}/transitions`  | Change the status (write)                                 |
| POST      | `/issues/{key}/assign`       | Assign or unassign (write)                                |
| GET       | `/issues/{key}/comments`     | Comments, oldest first                                    |
| POST      | `/issues/{key}/comments`     | Add a Markdown comment (write)                            |
| GET       | `/issues/{key}/time-entries` | Logged time                                               |
| POST      | `/issues/{key}/time-entries` | Log time (write)                                          |
| POST      | `/issues/{key}/attachments`  | Upload a file in the multipart field `file` (write)       |
| GET       | `/attachments/{id}`          | Download a file                                           |
| GET       | `/time-activities`           | Activities for time entries                               |
| GET       | `/search`                    | Text search; an exact key comes first                     |
| GET, POST | `/webhooks`                  | List or add webhooks (admin; write)                       |
| DELETE    | `/webhooks/{id}`             | Remove a webhook (admin; write)                           |

## List and filter issues

[Section titled “List and filter issues”](#list-and-filter-issues)

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/issues?assignee=me&status=open&sort=-updated&per_page=100"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/issues?updated_since=2026-10-29T12:00:00Z&status=all"
```

| Parameter              | Values                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `assignee`             | `me`, `none`, a user id or an e-mail                                                                          |
| `reporter`, `watching` | `me`                                                                                                          |
| `status`               | `open` (not done), `closed`, `all`, a status id or a name                                                     |
| `project`              | A key, or several separated by commas (`WEB,AGENT`)                                                           |
| `type`, `priority`     | An option id, or several separated by commas                                                                  |
| `label`                | A label name                                                                                                  |
| `q`                    | Text in the title or description, or an exact key                                                             |
| `updated_since`        | An ISO 8601 timestamp, for polling                                                                            |
| `sort`                 | `-updated` (default), `updated`, `-created`, `created`, `-priority`, `priority`, `key`, `-key`, `due`, `-due` |
| `per_page`, `page`     | Pagination                                                                                                    |

## Create an issue

[Section titled “Create an issue”](#create-an-issue)

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "$TRACKER/issues" -d '{
  "project": "WEB",
  "title": "Saved filters in the sidebar",
  "description": "Save the list filters under a name.\n\n- [ ] UI\n- [ ] API",
  "type": "feature",
  "priority": "medium",
  "labels": ["ui"],
  "assignee": "me",
  "status": "To do",
  "parent": "WEB-5",
  "estimate_hours": 4,
  "due_date": "2026-11-30"
}'
# 201 {"data": {"key": "WEB-9", …}}
```

Only `project` and `title` are required. Unknown label names are created in the project. The new issue gets the next number of its project.

## Update an issue

[Section titled “Update an issue”](#update-an-issue)

```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-9" -d '{"priority": "high", "labels": ["ui", "api"], "due_date": null}'
```

It accepts the same fields as create, except `project`. Only the fields present change, and each change is written to the issue’s history.

## Change the status

[Section titled “Change the status”](#change-the-status)

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-3/transitions"
# {"data":[{"id":"1","name":"To do","category":"todo","current":false},
#          {"id":"2","name":"In progress","category":"in_progress","current":false},
#          {"id":"3","name":"Review","category":"in_progress","current":true},
#          {"id":"4","name":"Done","category":"done","current":false}]}


curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-3/transitions" -d '{"status": "Done"}'      # or {"status": "4"}
```

## Assign

[Section titled “Assign”](#assign)

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-3/assign" -d '{"assignee": "me"}'     # "me", a user id, an e-mail, or null to unassign
```

## Comment

[Section titled “Comment”](#comment)

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-3/comments" -d '{"body": "## Done\n- LCP 1.6 s\n\n## How to check\n1. `npm run build`"}'
```

## Log time

[Section titled “Log time”](#log-time)

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/time-activities"
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-3/time-entries" -d '{"hours": 1.5, "comment": "Profiling", "date": "2026-10-29", "activity": "development"}'
```

`hours` is required, more than 0 and at most 24. `date` defaults to today and `activity` to `development`.

## Attachments

[Section titled “Attachments”](#attachments)

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F "file=@screen.png" "$TRACKER/issues/WEB-3/attachments"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o screen.png "$TRACKER/attachments/3"
```

## Search

[Section titled “Search”](#search)

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/search?q=login&project=WEB&limit=20"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/search?q=web-3"   # the exact key comes first
```

Search covers all statuses; pass `status=open` to narrow it.

## Projects and create metadata

[Section titled “Projects and create metadata”](#projects-and-create-metadata)

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/projects"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$TRACKER/projects/WEB/meta"
# {"data":{"types":[{"id":"task","name":"Task"},…],"priorities":[…,{"id":"medium","name":"Medium","current":true},…],
#          "labels":[{"id":"1","name":"backend"},…],"statuses":[…],"members":[{"id":"1","name":"Ada Example"},…]}}
```

## Skribly Agent mapping

[Section titled “Skribly Agent mapping”](#skribly-agent-mapping)

The API is shaped after Skribly Agent’s `TrackerClient`, so a client maps one method to one call. `@skribly/core` names its client methods after the same operations.

| TrackerClient         | Call                                                                 | Notes                         |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `whoami()`            | `GET /me`                                                            | Returns `data.name`           |
| `mine()`              | `GET /issues?assignee=me&status=open&sort=-updated&per_page=100`     |                               |
| `get(key)`            | `GET /issues/{key}`                                                  | Comments included             |
| `comment(key, md)`    | `POST /issues/{key}/comments {body}`                                 | Markdown as is                |
| `statuses(key)`       | `GET /issues/{key}/transitions`                                      | Already `{id, name, current}` |
| `setStatus(key, id)`  | `POST /issues/{key}/transitions {status: id}`                        |                               |
| `assign(key, to)`     | `POST /issues/{key}/assign {assignee}`                               | `"me"`, `null` or an id       |
| `projects()`          | `GET /projects`                                                      | `{id: key, key, name}`        |
| `createMeta(project)` | `GET /projects/{key}/meta`                                           | Types, priorities, labels     |
| `create(input)`       | `POST /issues {project, title, description, type, priority, labels}` |                               |
| `logTime(key, entry)` | `POST /issues/{key}/time-entries {hours, comment, date, activity}`   |                               |
| `activities()`        | `GET /time-activities`                                               |                               |
| `search(q, project)`  | `GET /search?q=&project=`                                            |                               |

## OpenAPI

[Section titled “OpenAPI”](#openapi)

The OpenAPI 3.1 description is the source of the [API reference](/tracker/api/). `@skribly/core` keeps a copy and tests its client and schemas against it, so the contract, the client and these docs cannot drift apart silently.

# Self-hosting with Docker

> Run Skribly Tracker on your own machine or server with Docker Compose, or without Docker, and keep its data across restarts.

The Tracker ships with a Docker Compose stack: the app (PHP-FPM), nginx, MySQL 8.4, Vite for assets, and a queue worker that delivers webhooks.

Access

The repository is private for now, so cloning needs access to the Skribly organisation on GitHub.

## Start with Docker

[Section titled “Start with Docker”](#start-with-docker)

1. Clone the repository and create the environment file:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/skribly/tracker.git skribly-tracker
   cd skribly-tracker
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

2. Set a password for the administrator account before the first boot. Open `.env` and fill in `TRACKER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; the line above it names the administrator’s e-mail address.

3. Build and start the stack:

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d --build
   ```

4. Open `http://localhost:8100` and sign in as the administrator.

On the first boot the entrypoint generates the application key, waits for the database, runs the migrations and seeds a demo workspace with three projects, their issues, comments and time entries. Later restarts keep your data: seeding only runs while the database is empty.

Caution

Without `TRACKER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, a local install uses a demo password, and a production install (`APP_ENV=production`) refuses to seed. Never expose a demo install to the internet.

## Services

[Section titled “Services”](#services)

| Service         | Address                        | Notes                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Tracker (nginx) | `http://localhost:8100`        | Change with `TRACKER_PORT`                            |
| Vite            | `http://localhost:5174`        | Builds on save; `VITE_DEV_SERVER=true` for hot reload |
| MySQL 8.4       | Inside the Docker network only | Data in a named volume                                |
| Queue worker    | No port                        | Delivers webhooks: 3 tries, then gives up             |

nginx exposes a `/health` endpoint used by the container healthcheck. Uploaded files live in a named `app-storage` volume, so they survive rebuilds.

## Everyday commands

[Section titled “Everyday commands”](#everyday-commands)

```bash
docker compose logs -f app queue                 # follow the app and the webhook worker
docker compose exec app php artisan tracker:token you@example.com "Skribly Agent"
```
