```bash
docker compose exec app php artisan migrate      # after pulling a new version
docker compose down                              # stop; data stays in the volumes
docker compose down -v                           # stop and delete all data
```

## Without Docker

[Section titled “Without Docker”](#without-docker)

You need PHP 8.4, Composer and Node.js 22.

```bash
cp .env.example .env          # set DB_* or DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
composer install && npm install && npm run build
php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate --seed
php artisan serve
php artisan queue:work        # in a second terminal, for webhooks
```

## Running it for a team

[Section titled “Running it for a team”](#running-it-for-a-team)

* Set `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false` and `APP_URL` to the public address.
* Put the Tracker behind HTTPS. Tokens travel in the `Authorization` header.
* Change the database passwords in `.env` from the example values.
* Keep the queue worker running, or webhooks are never delivered.
* Back up the database volume and the storage volume.

All settings are listed in [Configuration](/tracker/configuration/).

## Upgrading

[Section titled “Upgrading”](#upgrading)

```bash
git pull
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose exec app php artisan migrate --force
```

Every push to `main` of the Tracker repository publishes a GitHub Release with notes grouped from the commits. See the [changelog](/changelog/).

# Personal access tokens

> Create, scope, use and revoke the personal access tokens that authenticate scripts, Skribly Agent and agent-skills against the Skribly Tracker API.

Every request to the REST API carries a personal access token as a bearer token. A token belongs to one person and acts with that person’s role.

## Create a token

[Section titled “Create a token”](#create-a-token)

In the browser: **Profile and API tokens → API tokens** (`/profile#tokens`).

1. Enter a name that says where the token is used, for example “Skribly Agent” or “CI”.

2. Choose the abilities:

   * **Read and write**: abilities `read` and `write`. Needed by Skribly Agent and to post comments from agent-skills.
   * **Read only**: ability `read`. Enough to fetch issues.

3. Optionally set an expiry date.

4. Copy the token. **It is shown once.**

From the command line on the server:

```bash
docker compose exec app php artisan tracker:token you@example.com "Skribly Agent"
docker compose exec app php artisan tracker:token you@example.com ci --read-only
```

A token looks like `1|` followed by 40 characters.

## What a token may do

[Section titled “What a token may do”](#what-a-token-may-do)

A token can never do more than its owner:

| Owner’s role | With `read`                        | With `read` and `write`                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Viewer       | Read everything the viewer can see | Same as read only                                                                      |
| Member       | Read                               | Create and change issues, comment, assign, change status, log time, upload attachments |
| Admin        | Read                               | Everything a member can do, plus webhooks                                              |

Endpoints that change data need the `write` ability. Deleting an issue also needs the owner to be an admin or the issue’s reporter. A request that the token’s ability or the owner’s role does not allow gets `403`.

## Use a token

[Section titled “Use a token”](#use-a-token)

```bash
export TRACKER=http://localhost:8100/api/v1
export TOKEN='1|…'
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/json" "$TRACKER/me"
```

`GET /me` returns the owner and the token’s abilities:

```json
{ "data": { "id": 1, "name": "Ada Example", "email": "ada@example.com", "role": "admin", "locale": "en", "abilities": ["read", "write"] } }
```

| Client          | Where the token goes                                                                          |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skribly Agent   | **Settings → Task trackers → Add tracker → Skribly Tracker**, URL and a read-write token      |
| agent-skills    | `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_URL` and `SKRIBLY_TRACKER_TOKEN` in `~/.config/agent-skills/credentials.env` |
| `@skribly/core` | `createTrackerClient({ baseUrl, token })`; see [How apps connect](/core/connecting/)          |
| Your scripts    | The `Authorization: Bearer` header                                                            |

## Keep tokens safe

[Section titled “Keep tokens safe”](#keep-tokens-safe)

* Never commit a token, paste it in a chat or put it in `.tasks/`.
* Give each tool its own token, so you can revoke one without breaking the others.
* Use read-only tokens wherever nothing needs to change.
* Use an expiry date for tokens on shared machines and in CI.
* Revoke a token on the profile page as soon as you suspect it leaked.

Requests without a token, or with a revoked or expired one, get `401`. More than 240 requests a minute per user get `429`.

## Planned

[Section titled “Planned”](#planned)

Short-lived tokens for apps and agents, limited to chosen projects and actions and shown as a visible bot, are planned for the whole ecosystem. See [Ecosystem architecture](/overview/architecture/#planned-building-blocks).

# Webhooks and signing

> Receive Skribly Tracker events as signed JSON webhooks - the events, the payload, the headers, retries, and how to verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature.

A webhook sends a signed JSON `POST` to your URL when something happens to an issue. Admins add webhooks in **Settings → Webhooks** or through the API.

## Events

[Section titled “Events”](#events)

| Event             | When                                      | `data`                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issue.created`   | An issue is created                       | `{ issue }`, the full [issue object](/tracker/rest-api/#the-issue-object) |
| `issue.updated`   | Fields, the status or the assignee change | `{ issue }`                                                               |
| `issue.deleted`   | An issue is deleted                       | `{ issue: { key, title }, actor }`                                        |
| `comment.created` | A comment is added                        | `{ issue, comment: { id, author, body } }`                                |

A webhook can listen to some events and to one project, or to everything.

## Add a webhook

[Section titled “Add a webhook”](#add-a-webhook)

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" "$TRACKER/webhooks" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com/hooks/skribly", "events": ["issue.updated", "comment.created"], "project": "WEB"}'
# 201 … "secret": "…"   (shown once)
```

The response holds the signing secret. **It is shown once**, so store it where your receiver can read it. `GET /webhooks` lists webhooks and `DELETE /webhooks/{id}` removes one; both need an admin token with the `write` ability.

## The request

[Section titled “The request”](#the-request)

```http
POST /hooks/skribly
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: SkriblyTracker/0.1.0
X-Skribly-Event: issue.updated
X-Skribly-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the webhook secret>
X-Skryba-Event: issue.updated
X-Skryba-Signature: sha256=<same value>


{"id":"<uuid>","event":"issue.updated","sent_at":"2026-10-29T20:10:36+01:00","data":{"issue":{…}}}
```

| Field     | Meaning                                                  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`      | A UUID per delivery; use it to drop duplicates           |
| `event`   | The event name, the same as the `X-Skribly-Event` header |
| `sent_at` | ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset                        |
| `data`    | The event’s data, as in the table above                  |

New receivers should read `X-Skribly-Signature` and `X-Skribly-Event`. The `X-Skryba-*` pair carries the same values and stays for receivers written before the rename.

## Delivery and retries

[Section titled “Delivery and retries”](#delivery-and-retries)

Deliveries are queued and sent by the queue worker:

|         |                                               |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Tries   | 3                                             |
| Backoff | 10 seconds, then 60 seconds                   |
| Timeout | 5 seconds per try (`TRACKER_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT`) |
| Success | Any `2xx` answer                              |

Answer quickly with `2xx` and do the work afterwards. If the queue worker is not running, nothing is delivered.

## Verify the signature

[Section titled “Verify the signature”](#verify-the-signature)

The signature is `sha256=` followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the **raw request body**, keyed with the webhook secret. Compute it over the bytes you received, never over a re-serialised object, and compare in constant time.

### Node.js, no dependencies

[Section titled “Node.js, no dependencies”](#nodejs-no-dependencies)

```js
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto'


export function verify(rawBody, signatureHeader, secret) {
  const expected = 'sha256=' + createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex')
  const given = String(signatureHeader ?? '')
  return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(given), Buffer.from(expected))
}
```

### With `@skribly/core`

[Section titled “With @skribly/core”](#with-skriblycore)

```ts
import { parseWebhookBody, verifyWebhookRequest } from '@skribly/core/webhooks'


if (verifyWebhookRequest(rawBody, request.headers, secret)) {
  const delivery = parseWebhookBody(rawBody)
  if (delivery.event === 'issue.updated') console.log(delivery.data.issue.key)
}
```

`verifyWebhookRequest` reads either header pair, and `parseWebhookBody` validates the payload against the shared [contract](/core/contracts/).

### PHP

[Section titled “PHP”](#php)

```php
$expected = 'sha256=' . hash_hmac('sha256', file_get_contents('php://input'), $secret);
$valid = hash_equals($expected, $_SERVER['HTTP_X_SKRIBLY_SIGNATURE'] ?? '');
```

### Python

[Section titled “Python”](#python)

```python
import hashlib, hmac


def verify(raw_body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature or "")
```

## Planned

[Section titled “Planned”](#planned)

Sending events in the shared CloudEvents envelope, which `@skribly/core` already defines, and signing in the Standard Webhooks style, with a timestamp in the signature and secret rotation, are planned. Receivers that use `verifyWebhookRequest` and `parseAnyWebhookBody` from `@skribly/core` already read both formats. See [Events](/core/events/).

# UI

> @skribly/ui, the shared look of Skribly: design tokens, plain CSS classes for any page, React components on React Aria and the Astro site kit of the Skribly sites, with light, dark and high contrast themes. Every component is live at ui.skribly.pl.

`@skribly/ui` is the shared look of Skribly: one set of design tokens, plain CSS for any page, React components for the apps, and the site kit of the Skribly websites.

See every component live

[ui.skribly.pl](https://ui.skribly.pl) is the live gallery of `@skribly/ui`: every component with working examples, in every theme.

## Layers

[Section titled “Layers”](#layers)

| Layer      | Files                                                                                                                     | Works in                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Tokens     | `tokens/*.tokens.json` in the W3C Design Tokens format, built by Style Dictionary into `tokens.css` and TypeScript values | Everything                  |
| Styles     | `components.css`, plain `.sk-*` classes in a cascade layer                                                                | Astro, plain HTML, anything |
| Components | React 19 on React Aria Components                                                                                         | The apps                    |
| Site kit   | Astro components, `site.css` and small TypeScript scripts                                                                 | The Skribly websites        |

A later framework change only replaces the top layer. React Aria supplies keyboard, focus and screen reader behaviour; the look stays Skribly’s.

## Use it

[Section titled “Use it”](#use-it)

With Tailwind 4:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@skribly/ui/styles.css";
```

```tsx
import { Button, Logo } from '@skribly/ui'
```

On a page with no Tailwind and no React:

```css
@import "@skribly/ui/plain.css";
```

```html
<button class="sk-button sk-button--outline">Cancel</button>
```

An app adds its own font link: Inter for the interface, JetBrains Mono for code, Bricolage Grotesque for display headings.

## Themes

[Section titled “Themes”](#themes)

Set `data-theme` to `light`, `dark` or `contrast` on the root, or on any element to theme only that part of the page. With no attribute on the root, the operating system decides, including `prefers-contrast: more`.

`data-density="compact"` gives the smaller controls and text of the desktop Agent. The `a11y-reduce-motion` and `a11y-strong-focus` classes on the root match the reader settings of the apps, and `prefers-reduced-motion` works with no class.

This site follows the same rules: pick **Light**, **Dark**, **High contrast** or **System** in the theme switch in the header. The choice holds on every Skribly site.

## Tokens

[Section titled “Tokens”](#tokens)

| Group             | CSS variables                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Surfaces          | `--sk-bg`, `-surface`, `-sunken`, `-side`, `-bar`, `-input`, `-hover`, `-selected` |
| Text and lines    | `--sk-fg`, `-muted`, `-border`, `-border-strong`                                   |
| Accent            | `--sk-accent`, `-strong`, `-fg`, `-text`, `-soft`, `-ring`                         |
| Status            | `--sk-danger`, `-warn`, `-ok`, `-info`, each with `-fg` and `-soft`                |
| Dark sidebar      | `--sk-nav`, `-fg`, `-muted`, `-hover`, `-active`, `-accent`                        |
| Product colours   | `--sk-tool-agent`, `-tracker`, `-skills`, `-docs`, `-ui`                           |
| Type              | `--sk-text-label`, `-caption`, `-body`, `-title`, `-heading`, `-page`, `-display`  |
| Sizes             | `--sk-space-*`, `--sk-control-sm`, `-md`, `-lg`                                    |
| Radius and shadow | `--sk-radius-sm` to `-xl`, `-full`; `--sk-shadow-sm` to `-lg`                      |
| Motion            | `--sk-duration-fast`, `-base`, `-slow`; `--sk-ease-out`, `-in-out`                 |
| Layers            | `--sk-z-sticky`, `-sidebar`, `-modal`, `-toast`, `-tour`                           |

Amber is the one accent. Green is for success only and red for destruction only. `--sk-accent-text` is the accent for text, because the plain accent fails 4.5:1 as a text colour on some surfaces. The package’s tests check every text and control pairing against WCAG contrast in all three themes.

## Plain classes

[Section titled “Plain classes”](#plain-classes)

Every class sits in the `components` cascade layer and reads only `--sk-*` tokens, so the themes, `data-density` and the reader settings work as they do in the apps, and a page’s own CSS wins with no specificity fights. Each class has hover, focus and disabled states where they apply, and reads ARIA states such as `aria-current`, `aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-sort` and `aria-invalid` for the rest. Message tones pair their colour with a glyph.

| Group      | Classes                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Actions    | `.sk-button` (`--outline`, `--ghost`, `--danger`, `--sm`, `--lg`, `--icon`), `.sk-link`, `.sk-kbd`                                                                         |
| Forms      | `.sk-field`, `.sk-fieldset`, `.sk-label`, `.sk-required`, `.sk-optional`, `.sk-hint`, `.sk-input`, `.sk-textarea`, `.sk-select`, `.sk-checkbox`, `.sk-radio`, `.sk-switch` |
| Messages   | `.sk-error`, `.sk-status`, `.sk-alert`, `.sk-callout`, `.sk-badge`                                                                                                         |
| Progress   | `.sk-spinner`, `.sk-progress`                                                                                                                                              |
| Data       | `.sk-table-wrap`, `.sk-table` (`--compact`, `--stack`)                                                                                                                     |
| Navigation | `.sk-nav`, `.sk-tabs`, `.sk-breadcrumbs`, `.sk-pagination`, `.sk-skip-link`                                                                                                |
| Overlays   | `.sk-dialog`, `.sk-tooltip`, `.sk-details`                                                                                                                                 |
| Content    | `.sk-prose`, `.sk-code`, `.sk-divider`, `.sk-avatar`, `.sk-card`, `.sk-visually-hidden`                                                                                    |
| Layout     | `.sk-container`, `.sk-stack`, `.sk-cluster`, `.sk-grid`, `.sk-hero`                                                                                                        |

The markup carries the meaning and the classes only the look: a checkbox is a `<label>` around its `<input>`, an error is linked with `aria-describedby`, and a table wider than the screen sits in `.sk-table-wrap` with `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"` and a name.

## Site kit

[Section titled “Site kit”](#site-kit)

The site kit gives skribly.pl, docs.skribly.pl and ui.skribly.pl one technology, Astro 7, and one set of parts, so they look and behave as one. This documentation site already runs on it; skribly.pl and ui.skribly.pl are moving onto it.

* One header with the Skribly products switcher, which shows the logo of every product: Skribly, Skribly Agent, Skribly Tracker, agent-skills, Skribly Docs and Skribly UI.
* One theme switch: light, dark, high contrast or the system’s choice. The choice is kept in the `sk-theme` cookie on `.skribly.pl`, so it holds on all three sites.
* One accessibility panel: text size, grayscale, high contrast, inverted colours, light background, underlined links, a readable font, stopped animations and a strong focus ring, kept the same way in the `sk-a11y` cookie.
* One search dialog on Pagefind, opened with `Ctrl`+`K`, `⌘`+`K` or `/`.
* One footer, skip link, breadcrumb trail and 404 page, and one title pattern: `<page> | Skribly <site>`.
* The same meta description, canonical address, Open Graph card and structured data on every page.
* Motion that stops when you ask for less: pages change with a view transition, headings rise in and sections lift into view, all off under reduced motion or the panel’s **Stop animations**.

The sites do not install the private repository. Each keeps a copy in `vendor/skribly-ui`, written by one command in the UI repository, and its tests fail when the copy is edited by hand.

## Components

[Section titled “Components”](#components)

The components come in groups, and each group also has its own entry point, such as `@skribly/ui/forms`. As of 8 November 2026 the main branch has:

| Group        | Examples                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Theme        | `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeToggle`, `AccessibilitySettings`, `SkipLink`, `LiveRegion`, `VisuallyHidden`                 |
| Brand        | `Logo`, `Wordmark`, `AppLockup`, `Avatar`, `AgentChip`, `TrackerBadge`                                              |
| Actions      | `Button`, `IconButton`, `LinkButton`, `ToggleButton`, `CopyButton`, `Kbd`, `KeyCombo`                               |
| Forms        | `TextField`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `DateInput`, `FileInput`, `FormErrorSummary` |
| Feedback     | `Alert`, `Badge`, `Banner`, toasts, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `ProgressBar`, `Meter`                     |
| Overlays     | `Modal`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `InfoTip`                                           |
| Navigation   | `Tabs`, `LinkTabs`, `Segmented`, `Breadcrumbs`, `Pagination`, `FilterChips`, `LanguageSwitch`                       |
| Surfaces     | `Card` and its parts, `StatCard`, `Hero`, `SettingsSection`, `OptionCard`, `Divider`                                |
| Data         | `Table`, `DataTable`, `List`, `VirtualList`, `TreeView`, `Timeline`, `KeyValueList`                                 |
| Shell        | `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `Topbar`, `StatusBar`, `SplitView`, `Pane`, `Dock`                                          |
| Search       | `CommandPalette`, `GlobalSearch`, `QuickOpen`, `Highlight`                                                          |
| Content      | `Markdown`, `CodeBlock`, `Snippet`, `TerminalScreen`, `Prose`                                                       |
| Conversation | `MessageThread`, `MessageBubble`, `Composer`, `ToolLine`, `CommentItem`, `CommentForm`                              |
| Onboarding   | `Tour`, `TourSpotlight`, `Checklist`, `OnboardingSteps`                                                             |
| Charts       | `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `StackedBars`, `DonutChart`, `ActivityHeatmap`, `Sparkline`, `ScoreRing`, `MetricTile`     |
| Media        | `UploadDropzone`, `MediaGrid`, `MediaPicker`, `ImageEditor`, `ImageField`                                           |
| Tracker      | `Board`, `TaskCard`, `IssueRow`, `IssueTable`, `IssueKey`, `PriorityBadge`, `LabelList`                             |
| Code         | `GitFileRow`, `GitGraph`, `CommitBox`, `PullRequestCard`, `EditorStatusBar`, `BrowserBar`                           |
| Pages        | `AuthLayout`, `LoginForm`, `PasswordResetForm`, `ErrorPage`                                                         |

The package has no tagged release yet, and no app uses these components so far.

Every component follows the same rules: semantic tokens only, so it is right in every theme; no built-in text, so every label, `aria-label` included, comes from the app’s own language files; never meaning carried by colour alone; and an axe check of every demo in every theme in the tests.

## Planned

[Section titled “Planned”](#planned)

* skribly.pl and ui.skribly.pl on the site kit.
* A tagged 0.1.0 release, then Skribly Agent and Skribly Tracker moving onto its components.
